section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Never — you must not go around a lowered gate.,b:When the train has passed and gates are up.,c:If the lights have stopped flashing but the gate is still down.,d:If an approaching train seems far away.
note: Do not drive around or under a lowered gate; you must wait until lights and bells stop and the gate is fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:You may pass from your lane when traffic is clear.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:Only if you are on an expressway.
note: If the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle under which conditions?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When a school bus's flashing red lights are on.,c:When approaching an intersection.,d:All of the above.
note: Never pass on hills or curves, at intersections, before or on railroad crossings or bridges, or when a stopped school bus has flashing red lights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:No — it has no effect on BAC.,b:Yes — it decreases BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you feel more alert but it does not lower your blood alcohol concentration or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes (five seconds on a freeway), check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder.,b:Rely only on mirrors without checking your blind spot.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,d:Signal after you start the lane change.
note: Begin signaling in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to clear blind spots before completing a lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can alcoholic beverages affect your driving ability?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking and give false confidence.,b:They always make you more alert.,c:They improve coordination in small amounts.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows reflexes, impairs judgment and coordination, and can create a false sense of confidence.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must a driver behave when encountering pedestrians?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them.,b:Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Assume pedestrians should yield to vehicles.,d:Proceed unless the pedestrian is in your lane.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is not lawfully crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or the vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs coordination, judgment, and reaction time; it reduces a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When, if ever, may you legally drive above the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never; posted limits are the maximum under ideal conditions.,b:When no police officer is present to enforce the limit.,c:When surrounding traffic is driving above the limit.
note: Speed limits represent the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you should not exceed them. You may need to go slower when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced and headlights are required from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.,b:Because traffic moves much faster at night.,c:Because there is always more traffic at night.
note: At night you cannot see as well; use headlights appropriately and drive so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an approaching train is close enough or traveling fast enough to be hazardous, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough to be a danger, do not attempt to cross the tracks. Wait until it has completely passed and all signals have cleared.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you finish the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:Either lane indiscriminately.
note: Turn into the lane nearest to the one you left—on a left turn to a one-way street, that will be the leftmost available lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a driver's left arm and hand extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:They intend to come to a stop.,b:They plan to turn left.,c:They plan to turn right.,d:They plan to speed up.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver intends to slow or stop; adjust your driving accordingly if following such a vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On traffic signals mounted horizontally, where is the red light located?
options: a:The rightmost position.,b:The middle position.,c:The leftmost position.
note: Horizontal signals place the red light on the left, yellow in the middle, and green on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only at stop signs.,b:Only at red lights.,c:Only if a police officer orders you to stop.,d:At stop signs, red lights, or when a traffic officer orders you to stop.
note: You must stop at intersections with stop signs or red lights and whenever a traffic officer instructs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What happens to your field of vision as your vehicle speed increases?
options: a:It decreases, requiring extra alertness for hazards.,b:It increases, letting you see more of the road.,c:It remains unchanged regardless of speed.
note: As speed increases, your peripheral vision narrows and you must be more alert to potential hazards ahead and to the sides.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What color are signs that indicate public recreation or cultural sites?
options: a:Green.,b:Brown.,c:Orange.
note: Brown signs indicate areas of cultural or historical interest or public recreation, useful when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view of other lanes, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly when the first lane clears.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Rely on another driver to wave you across.
note: Do not begin the left turn until you can see that all lanes you will cross are clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots.,b:Always use cruise control while changing lanes.,c:Stop on the shoulder to check traffic.
note: On interstates, signal and verify mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your lane.,b:Pass with caution whenever you want.,c:Slow down to below the speed limit.
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On slippery roads, how should you handle turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid the curve.,c:Accelerate quickly through curves.
note: Reduce speed before and during turns on slippery roads to maintain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which practice helps prevent \\highway hypnosis\\\" on long trips?\"
options: a:Begin the trip well-rested and take regular stops.,b:Drive continuously without stopping to maintain focus.,c:Keep the cruise control engaged at all times.
note: To avoid highway hypnosis, start well-rested, take regular breaks even if you don't feel tired, and keep your eyes scanning the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren or flashing lights, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but not stop.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.,d:Speed up to clear the lane.
note: You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle using warning devices.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at a railroad crossing under which circumstances?
options: a:When directed to do so by a flagger or a stop sign.,b:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.,c:Only if you see a train approaching.,d:Both a and b.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger or stop sign and when flashing red signals or gates are activated.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield, like a stop sign.,b:Proceed without stopping because the signal is broken.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red signal mandates a full stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you continue carefully through an intersection when the signal turns yellow?
options: a:If you are already in the intersection when the light turns steady yellow.,b:If there are pedestrians crossing.,c:If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
note: If you are already within the intersection when the light turns steady yellow, you should continue through carefully; do not enter on a yellow light if you can stop safely before the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you must:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn to warn other drivers.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted in either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway mean passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions except to turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and details of the accident.,b:Drive away if no one is nearby.,c:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.
note: If you cannot locate the owner after striking an unattended vehicle, leave a written notice with your contact information and the circumstances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For drivers 21 and older, at what BAC is driving illegal in Louisiana?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Louisiana law makes it illegal for drivers 21+ to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to use a three-point turn (turnabout)?
options: a:Only on a narrow street where a U-turn and going around the block are not possible.,b:Anytime you want to change direction quickly.,c:When driving in heavy, busy traffic.
note: Use a three-point turn only on a two-lane roadway when a U-turn is not possible and you cannot go around the block; it's the most difficult turnabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes into a solid green light, what applies to drivers who want to turn?
options: a:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You retain automatic right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives protected turn movement. If it becomes a regular green, you may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a turn, what action should you take?
options: a:Signal at least three to four seconds before turning.,b:Immediately turn the wheel without signalling.,c:Increase your speed then turn.
note: Activate your turn signal a few seconds before turning to notify other drivers and pedestrians of your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What happens if you refuse a requested alcohol analysis test in Louisiana?
options: a:Your license will be suspended (first offense results in 365-day suspension).,b:You face no consequences.,c:Refusal is recommended to avoid conviction.
note: By law, driving in Louisiana implies consent to chemical testing. Refusing a test results in administrative license suspension (365 days for a first refusal).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you find a defect that could affect safe vehicle operation, what should you do?
options: a:Drive only at reduced speeds until you can fix it.,b:Have the defect repaired immediately before driving.,c:Delay repairs until you can afford them.,d:Use the vehicle for short local trips only.
note: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be fixed as soon as possible and before driving when practical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No standing' sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may never stop your vehicle there.,b:You may park there if you remain in the vehicle.,c:You may stop only temporarily to load or unload passengers.
note: A No Standing sign means you can stop briefly to pick up or discharge passengers, but you may not park.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicles you are following.,b:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.,c:Approach all vehicles with caution.,d:All of the above.
note: In snowy or icy weather keep windows and mirrors clear, increase following distance, and approach other vehicles and hazards with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign showing Reduced speed - 35 mph means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.,b:The reduced speed zone begins at the next sign.,c:You have ample time to slow before the reduced speed starts.
note: A Reduced speed sign indicates the new speed limit takes effect at the sign; reduce speed accordingly at that point.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching railroad tracks, what actions should you take?
options: a:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before any approaching train arrives.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,d:Turn off your radio and keep moving normally.
note: Approach tracks with caution: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers depress the gas pedal?
options: a:Gradually and smoothly.,b:By lightly tapping it.,c:Abruptly to accelerate quickly.,d:With the heel lifted off the floor at all times.
note: Accelerate gradually and smoothly with the top of your foot on the gas pedal and your heel on the floor to maintain control.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?
options: a:Drive only on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your path.,c:Communicate your intentions to other road users (signal, brake, and position your vehicle clearly).
note: To help prevent crashes, make your actions predictable to others. Use turn signals, brake lights, eye contact when possible, and appropriate lane position so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians can anticipate what you will do and adjust safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you maintain?
options: a:A safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.,b:Decrease your following distance to fit into traffic.,c:Come to a complete stop before changing lanes.,d:Signal only after beginning the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, keep a safe following distance so you have time and space to react if traffic slows or stops. Then check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal before smoothly moving into the next lane.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Most general warning signs are yellow and often diamond-shaped with black symbols or words. They alert you to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other hazards ahead so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: As alcohol concentration in the blood increases, it generally:
options: a:Makes you more cautious and less confident.,b:Improves night vision.,c:Slows reactions and impairs judgment and coordination.
note: As blood alcohol concentration increases, your reaction time slows, your judgment and coordination worsen, and you become less able to notice and respond to hazards. Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce your ability to drive safely.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:You must stop and back up immediately.,b:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and possible changed traffic patterns; slow down and use caution.,c:That it is summer.
note: Work zone signs, usually orange with black symbols or words, warn that road work is ahead and driving conditions or traffic patterns may change. You should slow down, follow posted instructions, and be prepared for workers, equipment, and sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, what is important to do?
options: a:All of the above,b:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,d:Check your blind spot before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, you must signal in advance, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and make sure the lane is clear before moving. All of these steps work together to prevent collisions with vehicles you may not initially see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with heavy oncoming traffic while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and block it until traffic clears.,b:Wait in the intersection or behind the crosswalk as appropriate until it is safe to turn.,c:Use the next intersection regardless of traffic signal rules.
note: At a green light with heavy oncoming traffic, you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. You may move into the intersection when allowed in your state and wait with wheels straight until traffic clears, then complete the left turn only when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the roadway to let traffic pass when safe.,b:Continue at the same slow speed as you have the right to do.,c:Try to block the passing lane to prevent others from passing.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, if you are driving so slowly that traffic is building up behind you, you should safely pull off the roadway or into a turnout when possible and let other vehicles pass. This reduces driver frustration and helps keep traffic flowing smoothly.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:Human error.,c:New drivers.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, such as inattention, misjudging gaps or speed, following too closely, or driving too fast for conditions. While weather and road conditions matter, driver decisions and mistakes are the primary cause of most collisions.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They are harder to see and more vulnerable in traffic.,c:They always follow different traffic laws.
note: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are smaller, harder to see, and have little or no protection in a crash. Because they are more vulnerable to serious injury, drivers must scan carefully, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield when required to help keep them safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to enter a freeway from an acceleration lane?
options: a:Drive slowly to better observe traffic and then merge.,b:Signal,c:Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, signal, and merge while yielding to traffic already on the freeway.
note: When entering a freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic, signal your intention to merge, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not drive slowly in the acceleration lane, and do not expect freeway traffic to yield to you; the merging driver is responsible for adjusting speed and merging safely.

question: A flashing red light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to others, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Proceed through at normal speed.,d:Turn right only.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in or close to the intersection, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, let them pass, and try to create distance.,b:Retaliate by tailgating to discourage them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: When another driver is aggressive, your goal is to avoid a confrontation and reduce risk. Do not make eye contact, do not respond with gestures or aggressive driving, and allow the driver to pass you. Slow slightly if needed and create as much space as possible between your vehicle and theirs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an approaching traffic light turns solid yellow as you near an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,c:Ignore it and proceed as normal.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking abruptly.

question: If you are involved in a traffic accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Continue driving if no one looks hurt.,b:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,c:Leave the scene and report it later.
note: If you are involved in a collision, you are legally required to stop at or as close as possible to the scene without blocking traffic more than necessary. Once stopped, check for injuries, move vehicles out of traffic if you can do so safely, and exchange information and render aid as required by law.

question: Drivers may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant in Louisiana?
options: a:30 feet.,b:20 feet.,c:15 feet.
note: Parking too close to a fire hydrant can block firefighters from quickly connecting hoses in an emergency. In Louisiana, you must leave at least 15 feet of space on all sides of a fire hydrant when parking so emergency vehicles have clear access.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: When your car begins to skid, you should look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering "into the skid." As the tires regain traction, gently straighten the wheel and avoid sudden braking or acceleration to maintain control.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the 'P' stand for?
options: a:Prepare to pass.,b:Plan a route.,c:Pull over.,d:Predict.
note: SIPDE is a defensive driving strategy: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, Execute. The "P" stands for "Predict"—you mentally anticipate what other drivers, pedestrians, and road conditions might do next so you can be ready with a safe response.

question: Which description about work zones is correct?
options: a:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:Work zones may be moving or stationary and require extra caution.
note: Work zones can be either stationary (like a fixed construction area) or moving (such as a line-painting crew). They are marked with orange signs and devices. Drivers must slow down, follow posted work zone speed limits, and use extra caution because workers and equipment may be close to traffic.

question: What do pentagonal signs (five-sided) typically indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones or school crossings.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see a pentagonal sign, be prepared to slow down, watch for children, and obey any crossing guards or additional school-related warnings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are separated by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, and red is not used to separate opposing traffic lanes.

question: When pedestrians are in marked crosswalks, which is true?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:No one has the right-of-way.,c:Pedestrians must always be given the right-of-way.,d:Only emergency vehicles must yield.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. When a pedestrian is in a crosswalk, you must slow or stop as needed to let them cross safely, regardless of whether the crosswalk is at an intersection or mid-block.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are placed on the left side of the road and mark the beginning of a no passing zone. They warn you that passing other vehicles is not allowed in that area.

question: Which statement is true about even a small amount of alcohol?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol above the legal limit affects driving.,b:Alcohol has no effect on concentration.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reactions and harm your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Because these skills are critical for safe driving, any drinking before driving increases crash risk.

question: What seasonal hazard is common in autumn?
options: a:Only an increase in daylight hours.,b:Decreased need for following distance.,c:Slick leaves on roadways.
note: In autumn, fallen leaves—especially when wet—can make the road as slippery as ice. Reduce your speed, avoid hard braking, and increase following distance when driving over leaf-covered pavement.

question: What is the maximum distance you may be parked from a curb when parallel parking (Louisiana)?
options: a:You must be within 10 inches of the curb.,b:You must be within 15 inches of the curb.,c:You must be within 18 inches of the curb.
note: When parallel parking in Louisiana, your vehicle’s wheels must be no more than 18 inches from the curb. Being closer is fine, but beyond 18 inches is considered improperly parked and can be unsafe for traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can kill.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Speeding is dangerous for every driver, regardless of skill, because higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. Driving too slowly can also be hazardous if you block traffic, but the most clearly true and universally taught statement is that speeding can kill.

question: How do bridges and overpasses behave in winter weather?
options: a:They freeze after other roads.,b:They are unaffected by freezing temperatures.,c:They tend to freeze before and remain icy longer than other roadways.
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces because cold air surrounds them from above and below. They also tend to stay icy longer, so you should slow down and avoid sudden braking or steering when crossing them in cold weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,b:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,c:Continue to the next exit and then safely return to your desired route.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, keep driving to the next exit. Get off there, then safely find your way back. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the interstate or shoulder, because that creates a serious crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat an intersection protected by a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Stop as you would at a stop sign and proceed when safe.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles and pedestrians, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

question: If your vehicle does NOT have ABS and you must stop quickly, you should:
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down continuously.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Firmly pump the brake pedal.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should use the "pump and steer" method in an emergency stop. Firmly pressing and releasing the brake pedal repeatedly helps prevent the wheels from locking, which lets you maintain steering control and reduces the chance of skidding.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. Using the right edge line as a guide helps you avoid being blinded while still keeping your vehicle correctly positioned until the other car passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At intersections.,c:At railroad crossings.,d:All of the above.
note: Passing is unsafe and generally illegal at hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings because your view of oncoming traffic or crossing traffic is limited. You must not move into the opposing lane where you cannot clearly see that it is safe to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which general rule should you remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow traffic as quickly as possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Safe drivers match the general flow of traffic within the speed limit and only pass when it is truly necessary and clearly safe. Passing should not be done aggressively or routinely; it always carries extra risk because you enter another lane, often into oncoming traffic.

question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Following too closely.,b:Inattentive driving.,c:Excessive speed for conditions.,d:All of the above.
note: Common crash causes include following too closely, not paying attention, and driving too fast for conditions. Any of these behaviors can easily lead to a collision, so you must leave enough following distance, stay focused on the road, and adjust your speed to traffic, weather, and road conditions.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They rarely use headlights.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,c:They are smaller and harder to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are much smaller than cars and can be easily hidden in blind spots or blend into traffic, especially in mirrors or at intersections. Because they are harder to see and their speed and distance can be difficult to judge, drivers must look carefully and double-check for motorcycles before changing lanes or turning.

question: What factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:How much water they drank earlier.,b:Amount of food in the stomach,c:Only the drinker's tolerance.,d:Whether they are driving a manual or automatic vehicle.
note: The way alcohol affects you depends on several factors, including how much you drink, how quickly you drink, your body weight, sex, and whether you have food in your stomach. Food can slow the absorption of alcohol into the bloodstream, but it does not prevent impairment. Even with food, alcohol still reduces your judgment, reaction time, and coordination, so you must never rely on food to make drinking and driving safe.

question: How would you describe distracted driving?
options: a:Not a serious concern.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers and others.,c:Very uncommon.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, such as texting, eating, adjusting controls, or looking away from the road. It is extremely risky because even a brief distraction can cause you to miss hazards, drift out of your lane, or fail to stop in time, putting you, your passengers, and others on the road in danger.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do with their following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in good conditions.
note: In rain, snow, fog, or other poor conditions, it takes longer to see hazards and to stop your vehicle. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while driving on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Continue to the next exit and use it to reach your destination.,c:Make a U-turn to get back to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, you must never stop, back up, cut across the median, or make a U-turn. Those actions are illegal and extremely dangerous at high speeds. Instead, continue driving to the next exit, leave the interstate safely, and then find a route that takes you back to your intended destination.

question: What danger does a leaking exhaust system present?
options: a:Fumes can make you drowsy or cause death.,b:It causes excessive oil use.,c:It requires a tune-up sooner than normal.
note: A leaking exhaust can let poisonous gases like carbon monoxide enter the passenger area. These fumes have no smell and can make you drowsy, confused, or even cause death, especially in enclosed spaces or when idling. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: How should you check blind spots to avoid collisions?
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move.,c:Honk your horn right before changing lanes.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are areas called blind spots that you can only see by turning your head. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in your blind spot.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest relative speed to maintain?
options: a:Drive significantly slower than traffic to stay cautious.,b:Constantly vary speed to remain alert.,c:Drive faster than traffic to reduce time on the road.,d:Drive with the general flow of traffic within the posted limit.
note: Driving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic increases the chance of a collision because other drivers must constantly adjust to you. The safest practice is to drive with the general flow of traffic while staying at or below the posted speed limit and adjusting for road and weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle that is larger has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,d:The vehicle approaching from the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), drivers who arrive at the same time must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first and prevents confusion and collisions when there is no traffic control device.

question: When should vehicle occupants fasten safety belts?
options: a:Only when making sharp turns.,b:Only when traveling faster than 55 mph.,c:Before you start driving—Louisiana law requires all occupants to be properly buckled.
note: Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Louisiana law requires that every occupant be properly buckled, and belts should be fastened before the vehicle starts moving so all occupants are protected at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout or rotary, drivers should:
options: a:Drive clockwise around the central island.,b:Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.,c:Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.
note: Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to traffic already circulating inside it and then enter when there is a safe gap. Once inside, vehicles travel counterclockwise around the central island in the United States.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane on a roadway, which is the correct practice?
options: a:You may stop to look up an address.,b:You should not stop; keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you entered the wrong ramp.,d:You may stop briefly to drop off passengers.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane for any reason other than an emergency or when required by traffic control. If you need to look up an address, drop off passengers, or correct a mistake, continue driving until you can safely pull off the road or reach the next exit or safe turn-around point.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may turn in the arrow's direction without caution.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,c:The arrow has no regulatory meaning.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending. It is like a circular yellow light for that direction: slow down and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so. Do not speed up to beat the light; complete the turn only if you are already in the intersection and cannot safely stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Speed up and re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots to be sure the lane is clear, then signal your intention and move into the passing lane. Pass safely at a legal speed and return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and there is plenty of space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the signal allows you to proceed.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or stop line and remain stopped until the signal changes or you are otherwise allowed to proceed. In many areas you may turn right on red after a full stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it.

question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger’s directions and slow down when instructed.,b:Follow whatever surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger.,c:Assume flaggers are optional and ignore them.
note: In construction zones, flaggers have the same authority as traffic signals or signs. You must follow their directions, even if they differ from normal rules, and slow down or stop when they signal you to. This protects both workers and drivers.

question: What is the proper method for looking while backing a vehicle?
options: a:Open your door to check behind you.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.
note: When backing, you should physically turn your head and shoulders and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see behind you. Mirrors and cameras are helpful, but you must not rely on them alone because they have blind spots.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade indicate what?
options: a:Drivers should bear to the left.,b:Drivers must stop immediately.,c:Drivers should bear to the right.,d:The road ahead is closed.
note: On barricades and object markers, the diagonal stripes point toward the direction you should move. If the stripes slope downward to the left, traffic should pass on the left side of the barricade. If they slope downward to the right, you should pass on the right.

question: What is the best practical way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive fast through puddles to clear water.,b:Keep cruise control on to maintain steady speed.,c:Use high beam headlights in rain.,d:Slow down when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent it is to slow down on wet roads and keep your tires in good condition with proper tread depth and inflation. High speeds, cruise control, and sudden moves increase the risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines the space you need to safely cross traffic?
options: a:Whether you signaled early enough.,b:Road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.,c:The presence of a stop sign only.
note: To cross traffic safely, you need a large enough gap based on how fast other vehicles are coming, the number of lanes you must cross, and road and weather conditions that affect how quickly you can accelerate. Poor conditions or heavier traffic require more space and time.

question: If your wheels run off the paved roadway onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Yank the steering wheel to force the tires back onto the road.,b:Brake hard and stop immediately.,c:Slow down gently and then steer back onto the pavement when safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gently while keeping the wheels straight. Once you’ve reduced speed and checked that it is safe, gradually steer back onto the pavement without jerking the wheel or braking hard.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the recommended course of action?
options: a:Lie down and sleep inside the car.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Stay in your car,d:Stand in the road to attract attention.
note: In a snowstorm, you are usually safest staying in your vehicle. It provides shelter and is easier for rescuers to see than a person on foot. Run the engine only occasionally for heat with a window slightly open and the exhaust pipe clear of snow to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.

question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:
options: a:Dangerous and requiring caution.,b:Appropriate places to park temporarily.,c:Safe to cross because trains are rare.
note: Railroad crossings must always be treated as potentially dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right of way. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all warning signs, signals, and gates before crossing the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?
options: a:When the car in front is waiting to turn left and it is legal and safe to use the shoulder.,b:When the shoulder is paved, clear, and state law allows passing on the right.,c:When the car in front is driving under the speed limit and you can legally pass in a marked lane.,d:When state law specifically permits shoulder use for passing and it can be done safely.
note: In many states, you may pass a left‑turning vehicle on the right using the shoulder only when it is specifically permitted, the shoulder is paved and clear, and you can do so safely without leaving the roadway. However, driving on the shoulder is generally restricted and often illegal for passing, so you must follow your state’s specific laws and posted signs.

question: Alcohol in the bloodstream primarily:
options: a:Has no effect on driving at low doses.,b:Slows reflexes and reaction time.,c:Wakes you up and improves focus.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. Even at low levels, it slows your reflexes and reaction time, reduces coordination, and impairs judgment, all of which make driving less safe.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:Beer lessens impairment compared to wine.,b:Wine reduces impairment compared to beer.,c:Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol consumed, not the type of beverage.
note: Impairment is determined by how much pure alcohol you consume and how quickly your body absorbs it, not by whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard drink of each has about the same amount of alcohol, so any of them can impair you equally if you consume the same amount of alcohol.

question: In fog, what should you do regarding speed and headlights?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit if visibility seems fine.,b:Turn on hazard lights and turn off low beams.,c:Use high beams to see further in fog.,d:Drive cautiously at reduced speed and use low beam headlights.
note: In fog, you should slow down and increase your following distance because visibility is reduced. Use low beam headlights; high beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Hazard lights are for stopped or emergency situations, not for normal driving in fog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the recommended practice?
options: a:Look over your shoulder through the rear window.,b:Rely solely on a backup camera.,c:Rely only on your mirrors.
note: When backing up, turn your body and look directly through the rear window so you can clearly see what is behind you. Mirrors and backup cameras can help, but they have blind spots and should never be your only source of information when reversing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Each driver should proceed only when it is their turn and it is safe to go.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness when driving faster on a wet roadway?
options: a:Tire traction decreases and risk of hydroplaning increases.,b:Water has no effect if your tires are good.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: On wet roads, as your speed increases, your tires have less time to push water out of the way. This reduces traction and increases the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and you can lose steering and braking control.

question: If you must drive in fog, what should you do first?
options: a:Use high beam headlights for better visibility.,b:Turn on hazard lights only.,c:Drive at the maximum speed limit.,d:Turn on low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always turn on your low beam headlights first and slow down. Low beams and fog lights aim light down toward the road, helping you see without creating glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can actually make it harder to see.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian crosswalks only.,b:Railroad crossings where you must yield to trains.,c:School zones.,d:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It means you must look and listen for trains, yield the right-of-way to any approaching train, and proceed only when you are sure it is safe. Trains cannot stop quickly, so drivers must be prepared to stop.

question: Which best describes driving as an activity?
options: a:An automatically easy task anyone can do without practice.,b:A complex skill that is mastered over time and requires attention.,c:Always very simple regardless of conditions.
note: Driving is a complex skill that takes time and practice to master. It requires constant attention, good judgment, and the ability to adjust to changing traffic, weather, and road conditions while following all traffic laws.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights if your vehicle has them. These lights reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off the fog and can make visibility worse.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving best described?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem that impairs safe driving.,b:A minor traffic safety issue if only a few drinks are consumed.,c:Safe as long as you feel okay to drive.
note: Drinking alcohol and driving is a serious safety hazard. Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce coordination, greatly increasing the risk of a crash for you and others on the road.

question: Which in-vehicle distraction increases crash risk the most?
options: a:Eating a sandwich quietly.,b:Playing the CD player.,c:Using a cell phone.,d:Listening to the radio.
note: Using a cell phone, even hands‑free, takes your attention away from the road visually, mentally, and often physically. This multitasking greatly increases crash risk compared with relatively simple background activities like quietly eating or listening to music.

question: What does an orange traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A construction or maintenance area.,c:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any posted directions.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks and you cannot free it, you should:
options: a:Shift to neutral, then turn off the ignition without locking the steering, apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe area.,b:Slam on the brakes while steering abruptly.,c:Open the hood immediately while driving to inspect the throttle.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle: shift to neutral, steer smoothly, and apply the brakes. Once you are in neutral and slowing, turn the ignition off without locking the steering wheel, then move off the road to a safe place and stop.

question: When a curb is painted yellow, what does that indicate?
options: a:Short parking stops only.,b:Accessible parking.,c:A loading zone or another parking restriction.
note: A yellow‑painted curb typically marks a loading zone or another limited‑stopping area. You may be allowed to stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or cargo, not for regular parking, and local signs will specify the exact restriction.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean for left turns?
options: a:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction immediately.,b:You must come to a complete stop.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow left‑turn arrow means you may turn left, but the turn is not protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic, cyclists, and pedestrians, and complete the turn only when there is a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:
options: a:The posted minimum speed limit.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,c:The posted maximum speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: You must never drive faster than is reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that means driving below the posted maximum speed limit. The posted maximum is the legal upper limit in ideal conditions, but in rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor roads you must slow down so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: What should drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger cars.,c:They need no extra space to turn compared to passenger cars.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all four sides, especially directly behind and along the right side, and they need more distance to stop and more room to turn and maneuver. Give them extra space, avoid lingering beside them, and don’t cut in front of them because they cannot stop as quickly as a passenger car.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs tell drivers?
options: a:They are placed only where a present danger exists.,b:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,c:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do under the law, such as speed limits, no parking, one-way, or no U-turn. They are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black or red lettering or symbols. You are legally required to obey these signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in a line at a stop sign and the cars ahead have cleared the intersection with no cross traffic, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping again.,b:Bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping the second time.,d:Honk and proceed.
note: At a stop sign, each driver must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, even if the car ahead has already stopped and gone through. After stopping, you must yield to any pedestrians and cross traffic before proceeding.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before maneuvers called?
options: a:A dangerous maneuver.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:Unnecessary scanning.,d:Checking your blind spot — a good driving habit.
note: Checking your blind spot by quickly turning your head before changing lanes, merging, or pulling away from a curb is an essential safe-driving habit. Mirrors do not show areas directly beside and slightly behind your vehicle, so a brief head check helps you spot vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians that you might otherwise miss.

question: Which actions improve safety when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and ensure headlights are functioning properly.,b:Drive if you are very tired but keep windows open.,c:Use only parking lights.,d:Turn on interior lights to read maps.
note: At night your visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge distance and speed. Increasing your following distance gives you more time to react if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Making sure your headlights are clean, properly aimed, and working on both low and high beam helps you see the road and be seen by others. Driving when very tired, using only parking lights, or turning on bright interior lights all reduce safety and should be avoided.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, certain medications (legal or illegal), and lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only physical injuries.
note: Alcohol, many prescription and over‑the‑counter medications, illegal drugs, and even extreme fatigue all slow your reaction time, affect judgment, and reduce coordination. Any of these can make you unsafe to drive, even if they are legal or were prescribed. You are responsible for knowing how what you consume affects your ability to drive and choosing not to drive if you are impaired.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,b:Stop and look for a train, remaining at least 15 feet from the nearest rail.,c:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.
note: Flashing lights at a railroad crossing mean a train is approaching. You must stop before the tracks, at least 15 feet from the nearest rail, and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and it is clearly safe to proceed. Never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train; trains are much faster and take far longer to stop than they appear.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:Smaller blind spots than passenger cars.,b:Increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:Decreased stopping distance compared to cars.,d:Less noise and vibration.
note: Heavy trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to come to a complete stop. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them and allow extra space so the truck driver has enough room to brake safely. Also stay out of their large blind spots along the sides and directly behind the truck whenever possible.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your seat belt.,c:Your seat position.
note: Adjust your seat position first so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls, and have a clear view of the road and mirrors. Once your seat is set, adjust the mirrors to minimize blind spots, then fasten and properly position your seat belt. If you change the seat later, you may need to readjust the mirrors.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Drive using only parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights (low beams) to increase visibility.,c:Use four-way flashers while moving.
note: At dusk, dawn, or on overcast days, visibility is reduced even if it is not fully dark. You should turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see and so other drivers can see you. Parking lights alone are not enough and are not legal to use as driving lights, and four‑way flashers are only for stopped or very slow‑moving vehicles in an emergency.

question: If you are involved in a collision, which of the following actions should you take?
options: a:Call the police or request emergency services if needed.,b:All of the above,c:Stop immediately.,d:Help the injured if you can.
note: If you are involved in a collision, you must stop immediately, help anyone who is injured if you can do so safely, and call the police or emergency services when needed. Failing to stop is a serious offense. All of these actions together are part of your legal and safety responsibilities after a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your turn signals are not working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use proper hand signals.,b:Use your horn.,c:Use your headlights.,d:Flash your brake lights repeatedly.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you are still required to signal your turns and lane changes. Use the standard hand and arm signals: left arm straight out for a left turn, left arm bent up for a right turn, and left arm bent down to indicate slowing or stopping. This lets other road users know your intentions.

question: Doubling a car's speed increases the force of impact by about how much?
options: a:Two times.,b:Depends only on vehicle weight.,c:Three times.,d:Four times.
note: The force of impact in a crash is related to the vehicle’s kinetic energy, which increases with the square of speed. If you double your speed, your vehicle has about four times as much kinetic energy, so the potential impact force and stopping distance are about four times greater. This is why even small increases in speed greatly increase crash severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane (the nearest appropriate lane).,b:The middle lane by default.,c:Any lane as long as you signal.,d:The far right lane only.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, you must turn into the nearest appropriate lane for your direction of travel. For example, a left turn should end in the leftmost lane going your way, and a right turn should end in the rightmost lane going your way. After completing the turn and ensuring it is safe, you can change lanes if needed.

question: What do diagonal stripes sloping down to the right on a barricade or panel tell drivers?
options: a:They indicate you must stop.,b:They indicate you should bear to the right.,c:They indicate you should bear to the left.
note: On barricades and vertical panels, the diagonal stripes show which side you should pass on. If the stripes slope down toward the right, you must pass to the right of the barricade. If they slope down toward the left, you must pass to the left.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Never; they must yield to you.,b:Whenever you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,c:Only when they are directly behind you.,d:Only if other vehicles have already yielded.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: Which statement about drowsy driving is true?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably prevent drowsiness.,b:Drowsy drivers can appear to be intoxicated due to poor driving.,c:Drinking strong coffee is an effective long-term solution.
note: Drowsy driving can seriously impair your judgment, reaction time, and vehicle control, and drowsy drivers often behave similarly to drunk drivers. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee do not reliably prevent drowsiness; the only safe solution is to rest before driving or stop and sleep if you become drowsy.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and that vehicle is to your right, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat them through the intersection.,b:Proceed and force the other vehicle to stop.,c:Honk and proceed.,d:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and let the vehicle on your right go first to avoid a collision and keep traffic moving safely.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you have lost control of your vehicle and to warn of immediate danger.,b:To signal your annoyance at a slow driver.,c:While passing another car on a two-lane road.,d:To express thanks after they yield.
note: Use your horn only to warn other road users when it is necessary for safety, such as when you lose control of your vehicle or when another driver or pedestrian is about to create an immediate hazard. Do not use the horn to express anger, impatience, or as a greeting.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you want to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to pass or change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop promptly.,c:Keep driving and let it pass on either side.,d:Accelerate to clear the intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as you safely can to the right side or curb and stopping until it has passed, unless otherwise directed by law enforcement.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do with your following distance?
options: a:Increase the following distance to allow more time to stop.,b:Keep the same following distance as on dry roads.,c:Decrease your following distance to keep traffic flowing.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. Increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react and brake smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you?
options: a:No passing is allowed.,b:The road is a one-way road.,c:The road is a two-way road with traffic moving in both directions.,d:The road is temporarily closed.
note: A yellow centerline means traffic on the road moves in opposite directions. A broken yellow line between lanes means passing is allowed in either direction when it can be done safely and is not otherwise prohibited.

question: What does fluorescent yellow-green sign color indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:Pedestrian,c:Hospitals.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green signs are used for pedestrian crossings, bicycle crossings, and school-related warnings. They alert drivers to areas with higher pedestrian or bicyclist activity so drivers can slow down and be prepared to yield.

question: If a vehicle is tailgating you and there's no right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase the gap.,b:When safe, gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to discourage tailgating.,d:Ignore them and maintain speed.
note: If someone is following too closely and you cannot move to the right, gradually slow down to increase the space in front of you and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Never slam on your brakes, because that can cause a rear-end collision, and do not speed up, because that reduces your reaction time and increases crash severity.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive more quickly to clear the hazardous area sooner.,b:Drive the posted speed limit exactly.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, you must reduce your speed so your tires can maintain traction. Slowing down gives you more time to react and shortens the distance you need to stop without skidding. Driving at or above the posted limit can be unsafe when conditions are poor, even if it is legal in dry conditions.

question: When driving under non-ideal conditions, what minimum following distance should you keep?
options: a:At least three seconds, and increase to four seconds or more in poor conditions.,b:One second.,c:Two seconds.
note: In good conditions, a minimum three‑second following distance is recommended so you have time to react if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. When conditions are not ideal—such as rain, fog, darkness, or heavy traffic—you should increase that gap to at least four seconds or more. More space gives you extra time to brake smoothly and avoid skids or collisions.

question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and drive through the intersection.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should do what?
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road and merge safely when possible.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Proceed without stopping if they think it's clear.,d:Have the right-of-way over traffic on the public road.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must yield to all vehicles and pedestrians already on the public road. They have the right‑of‑way. Wait until there is a safe gap in traffic, then merge smoothly without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking near a crosswalk, how close may you legally park to the crosswalk?
options: a:No closer than 10 feet.,b:No closer than 5 feet.,c:No closer than 20 feet.
note: You must not park too close to a crosswalk so drivers and pedestrians can see each other clearly. Many states, including Louisiana, prohibit parking within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, so you should leave at least that much space.

question: To ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe, you should:
options: a:Only drive when your physical condition is perfect.,b:Ignore side effects of medicines if you feel fine.,c:Know how any medicine affects your driving
note: Medicines, including some over‑the‑counter drugs, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. Always know how any medicine affects your ability to drive, and do not drive if it could impair you, even if you feel okay.

question: What should happen to your following distance when driving in snowy weather?
options: a:Keep it the same as in dry conditions.,b:Decrease it because vehicles stop faster in snow.,c:Increase it—allow more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
note: Snow and ice greatly increase stopping distance and reduce traction. You should increase your following distance so you have more time and space to brake gently and avoid skids or rear‑end collisions.

question: When are seat belts most effective?
options: a:All occupants in the vehicle should wear seat belts.,b:Passengers should wear seat belts only on long trips.,c:Only the driver should wear a seat belt.
note: Seat belts work best when everyone in the vehicle is buckled up. In a crash, unbelted passengers can be thrown around inside the car or ejected, and they can seriously injure others. All occupants should wear seat belts every trip, no matter how short.

question: How must drivers respond to a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Pass cautiously at slow speed.,b:Proceed if you think most children are done exiting.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Honk before passing the bus on the left.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in most situations must come to a complete stop and stay stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and it is clearly safe to move. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the right lane of the one-way street.,c:In the center of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street onto a one‑way street, you should turn into the lane closest to you on the one‑way street, which is the leftmost lane. This keeps your path short, predictable, and safe for oncoming and following traffic.

question: The Highway Transportation System consists of which main components?
options: a:People only.,b:Vehicles only.,c:People, vehicles, and roads.
note: The Highway Transportation System (HTS) is made up of people (drivers, pedestrians, cyclists), vehicles (cars, trucks, buses, etc.), and roadways. Safe driving depends on how well these three parts work together.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply away from the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll back slightly and the front tire will rest against the curb, helping stop the car from rolling into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions should you perform when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Signal,b:Check only your side view mirror.,c:Check only your rearview mirror.,d:Quickly turn your head without signaling.
note: Before changing lanes, you must signal to let other drivers know your intention, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Relying on only one mirror or not signaling is unsafe and often illegal.

question: On a horizontal traffic signal, which position is the green light in?
options: a:On the right.,b:In the middle.,c:On the left.
note: On a horizontal traffic signal, the lights are arranged from left to right as red, yellow, then green. That means the green light is on the right side, indicating when you are allowed to proceed if the way is clear.

question: What color combination do most warning signs use to indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white.,b:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,c:White letters on a blue background.
note: Warning signs that alert you to upcoming hazards are usually yellow with black symbols or lettering. These colors stand out and give drivers time to see and react to potential dangers ahead. Construction and maintenance warning signs use orange with black, but standard hazard warnings are yellow and black.

question: When are headlights legally required in Louisiana?
options: a:When the driver is tired.,b:When the temperature drops below freezing.,c:Between sunset and sunrise.
note: In Louisiana, you must use headlights between sunset and sunrise so other drivers can see you and you can see the road clearly. You must also use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle within 200 feet to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: You hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop when safe.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way. On a divided multilane highway, slow down, move to a position that gives the emergency vehicle a clear path, and stop if needed until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: How should a seat belt be positioned?
options: a:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and low on your pelvis.,b:Loose and comfortable.,c:Hidden beneath the seat cushion.
note: For best protection, the lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and low on your pelvis, not across your stomach. The shoulder belt should cross the center of your chest and rest on your shoulder, away from your neck. This positioning helps the belt hold your body’s stronger bones in a crash and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: What is road rage considered under the law?
options: a:Merely an annoyance.,b:A criminal offense that can lead to serious legal consequences.,c:An acceptable response to poor driving by others.
note: Road rage is aggressive or violent driving behavior that goes beyond simple discourtesy. When a driver uses a vehicle to threaten, intimidate, or harm others, it can be charged as a criminal offense, leading to fines, license suspension, or even jail time.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting with the engine running in drive.,b:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.,c:Accelerating quickly.
note: Looking ahead to avoid sudden stops and accelerating smoothly conserves fuel; hard accelerations and idling waste gasoline.

question: What does an \End school zone\" sign communicate?"
options: a:That the speed limit is 20 mph.,b:The end of a reduced-speed school zone.,c:The beginning of a reduced-speed school zone.
note: An \End school zone\" sign indicates the reduced school-zone speed limit is ending and the regular speed limit resumes."

question: You are about to back out of a driveway and see children playing nearby. Before moving your car you should:
