options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:Assume the children will hear you and back up slowly.,c:Walk to the back of the car and check that the way is clear.
note: When children are nearby, you should always walk to the back of your vehicle and check the area before backing. Small children can be hard to see in mirrors or cameras, and they may move unpredictably. Never rely on your horn or assume they will stay clear; physically checking behind the car is the safest practice.

question: How are smoking and preparing to smoke while driving classified?
options: a:Actions that help maintain alertness.,b:Activities that do not affect driving.,c:Distracting activities that can reduce safety.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction because it takes at least one hand off the wheel and can draw your eyes and attention away from the road. Handling lighters, matches, or dropped cigarettes further increases crash risk. Any activity that diverts your hands, eyes, or mind from driving is considered a distracting activity.

question: When may you legally cross solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction at any time.,b:Only when making a left turn or entering/exiting a driveway where permitted.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: A solid yellow centerline generally means you must not cross it to pass other vehicles. You may usually cross solid yellow lines only to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited. Passing across solid yellow centerlines is illegal in most situations because it puts you into oncoming traffic.

question: Why should you exercise extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.,b:They are a police officer.,c:They are signaling to stop traffic.,d:They are likely blind and may need the right-of-way and extra time to cross.
note: A white cane (often with a red tip) is used by people who are blind or visually impaired. When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop. They may not be able to see you or judge your speed, so giving them extra time and space is essential for their safety.

question: Which behavior is commonly associated with road rage?
options: a:Keeping a safe distance from other cars.,b:Flashing headlights to warn others.,c:Deliberately obstructing other vehicles.
note: Road rage involves aggressive or hostile driving actions intended to intimidate or interfere with others, such as deliberately blocking or obstructing another vehicle, tailgating, cutting off drivers, or making threatening gestures. Safe drivers avoid these behaviors, create space, and do not retaliate when confronted with aggression.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what documents must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance only.,b:Vehicle registration only.,c:Driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.
note: When an officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment check, you are generally required to show three things: your valid driver license, the vehicle’s current registration, and proof of financial responsibility (insurance). Keep these documents in the vehicle or on your person so you can present them promptly when requested.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Always stop and wait until all other vehicles have cleared the intersection.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed without slowing.,c:Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield according to right‑of‑way rules, including yielding to vehicles that arrive first or from your right.
note: At an intersection without signs or signals, you must approach with caution, slow down, and be prepared to stop. The general rule is to yield to vehicles that arrive first and to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time. Always adjust your speed so you can safely yield and avoid a collision.

question: When a curb is painted white, what does it indicate?
options: a:Accessible (disabled) parking only.,b:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time.,c:Passenger loading zone—stop only briefly to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.
note: A white painted curb usually indicates a passenger loading zone where you may stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers or mail, not for long‑term parking. Other colors have different meanings, such as yellow for loading zones and red for no stopping or parking. Always check for nearby signs that may give more specific time limits or restrictions.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Safely pull to the curb, stop, and look to see if the vehicle is approaching on your street.,b:Keep driving until you see the vehicle, then pull over.,c:Slow down but continue driving until you find it.
note: When you hear a siren and are not sure where the emergency vehicle is, you must still yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop, then look and listen to locate the vehicle. Stay stopped until you are sure the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to re‑enter traffic.

question: How should you pass an animal on the roadway if safe to do so?
options: a:Sound your horn repeatedly to scare it away.,b:Pass slowly and cautiously so you don't startle it.,c:Pass as closely as possible at normal speed.
note: When passing animals on or near the roadway, reduce your speed and move past them slowly and smoothly. Sudden movements, loud horn use, or passing too closely can startle animals and cause them to move unpredictably into your path. Give them extra space and be prepared to stop if they move toward the road.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes immediately.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery surface, sudden braking can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid. First, gently take your foot off the accelerator so the car slows down on its own. If you need to slow more, apply the brakes gently and steadily, avoiding hard or sudden pressure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one may proceed first.,c:The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left.,d:The larger vehicle always yields.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time from different roads, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals controlling the intersection.

question: Which light at an intersection indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A solid yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians. A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red and you should stop if you can do so safely. A flashing red light means stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.

question: What habits are important to maintain when driving on major highways?
options: a:Glance at one point on the road for long periods to avoid distraction.,b:Stay alert,c:Constantly drive at the same speed without scanning.
note: Staying alert on highways means continuously scanning the road, mirrors, and surroundings to avoid highway hypnosis and to spot hazards early. You should not stare at one point or drive on autopilot; instead, keep your eyes moving and be ready to react.

question: If a police officer stops you, what is the recommended behavior?
options: a:Get your paperwork out and show it before the officer approaches.,b:Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower the window.
note: If an officer stops you, the safest and recommended behavior is to stay in your vehicle, keep your hands clearly visible on the steering wheel, and wait for the officer to approach and give instructions. Only reach for your license, registration, and insurance when the officer asks you to, so they can clearly see your movements and know you are not a threat.

question: What color are highway destination and exit signs that show distances?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Red with white letters.,c:Yellow with black letters.,d:Black with white letters.
note: Highway guide signs that show destinations, exits, and distances are typically green with white letters or symbols. These signs help you identify routes, upcoming exits, and how far you are from cities or major points.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive and may lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer,b:Illegal drugs and certain prescription medications.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above
note: Driving under the influence laws apply to more than just beer or other alcoholic drinks. Illegal drugs, some prescription and over‑the‑counter medications, and inhalants like glue or paint can all affect your judgment, coordination, and reaction time. Any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely can lead to a DUI or similar charge.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when pulling toward a curb.,b:Whenever you are changing lanes or moving your vehicle's position.,c:Only when turning left or right at intersections.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You should quickly glance over your shoulder every time you change lanes, merge, or move your vehicle sideways (such as pulling to or from a curb) to make sure there is no vehicle, cyclist, or motorcycle in the blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light requires you to:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed slowly and with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down, look carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe. You are not required to stop, but you must use extra caution.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Open the window and drive on.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Get some coffee and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy, the only safe choice is to stop driving and rest or switch drivers. Opening a window or drinking coffee cannot overcome serious fatigue and can give a false sense of alertness, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: What should drivers do before starting a turn?
options: a:Immediately accelerate into the turn.,b:Always come to a complete stop before turning.,c:Slow down before making the turn.
note: Before turning, you should slow down to a safe speed so you can stay in your lane and maintain control throughout the turn. Entering a turn too fast can cause skidding, drifting out of your lane, or losing control of the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you to show you are waiting.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for it to clear.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Blocking the intersection can prevent cross traffic from moving and is illegal in many areas.

question: What is the meaning of fluorescent pink traffic signs?
options: a:Incident management signs.,b:School zone signs.,c:Speed limit signs.
note: Fluorescent pink signs are used for temporary incident management, such as crash scenes, emergency closures, or other nonpermanent events that affect normal traffic flow.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain when following a motorcycle?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles, and riders are more vulnerable in a crash. Leaving at least a four‑second following distance gives you extra time to react if the motorcycle stops suddenly, swerves to avoid a hazard, or falls.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line when:
options: a:Turning left into a driveway.,b:Passing a disabled vehicle in front of you.,c:Doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: A single broken line—white for same‑direction traffic or yellow for opposite‑direction traffic—may be crossed to pass or change lanes only when it is safe and legal. You must not cross if doing so would interfere with oncoming or adjacent traffic, force others to brake or swerve, or otherwise create a hazard.

question: When driving where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:That a child could run into the road without checking for traffic.,b:Children will always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Children will know when it is safe to cross.
note: Children are unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street without looking for traffic or understanding the danger. In areas where children may be present—near schools, parks, residential streets—you must slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop at any time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Only use the outside rearview mirror.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head to look over your shoulder and check the blind spot.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, signal, and then quickly turn your head to look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be hidden in your blind spot.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Motion for the vehicle to pass you on your left.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, continue through it, then pull over to the right and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the primary purpose of an advisory speed or speed restriction sign for curves and turns?
options: a:To be ignored in rainy,b:To indicate the sign is blue with black lettering.,c:To show a recommended safe speed for that curve or turn.
note: Advisory speed signs show a recommended safe speed for a specific curve or turn under ideal conditions. They are not enforceable like a speed limit sign, but you should slow to at least that speed and reduce your speed even more in rain, snow, or other adverse conditions.

question: What is meant by a truck's \No zone\"?"
options: a:A safety buffer that cars should drive in.,b:The blind spot around a large vehicle.,c:A designated no-passing zone.
note: A truck’s “No-Zone” is the large blind-spot area around a truck or other large vehicle where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Avoid driving or lingering in these areas, especially along the sides, directly behind, and close in front of the truck, because the driver may not know you are there and may not be able to react safely.

question: Which curb color indicates a fire zone where parking is restricted?
options: a:Blue.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.,d:White.
note: Red-painted curbs typically indicate a fire lane or fire zone where stopping, standing, or parking is not allowed, except when directed by authorities. These areas must be kept clear so emergency vehicles can access fire hydrants and buildings quickly.

question: Regulatory road signs are generally what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green.,b:White (many regulatory signs use a white background with black or red symbols, though some, like STOP and YIELD, use other colors).,c:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do or must not do, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. Many regulatory signs use a white background with black or red symbols or lettering, but some important regulatory signs, like STOP (red) and YIELD (red and white), use different colors. Regardless of color, regulatory signs must always be obeyed.

question: Which of the following is true about passing safely?
options: a:You need not signal if traffic is clear.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Return to your lane immediately after passing without checking.
note: To pass safely, signal well in advance (at least 100 feet before changing lanes in most areas), check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Pass only when it is legal and safe, and return to your lane only after you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

question: A solid white centerline on a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move opposite and passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and you may pass at will.
note: White lines always separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you should not change lanes unless it is necessary and safe, and in some locations lane changes are legally prohibited.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling nearby, what should you do to assist it?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop and prevent it from passing.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren on, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, or otherwise create a clear path so the vehicle can pass quickly and safely. Never speed up or block its path.

question: If taking a non-prescription drug, what should a driver do before driving?
options: a:Ignore labels and drive as usual.,b:Drink alcohol to counter side effects.,c:Read the labels for warnings about driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can cause drowsiness, dizziness, or slowed reaction time. Always read the label for warnings about driving and, if unsure, ask a doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking the medication.

question: What pavement markings or signals are sometimes used to direct drivers into proper turning lanes on highways?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road only.,b:No markings are used for this purpose.,c:Arrow markings on the pavement and lane-control arrows.,d:Flashing red lights above every lane.
note: Highways often use arrow markings painted on the pavement and overhead or roadside lane-control arrows to show which lanes are for turning and which are for through traffic. Drivers should be in the correct lane before reaching the intersection or exit.

question: What is the purpose of highway markings?
options: a:They are usually unimportant.,b:They provide information and guidance for drivers.,c:They are only for construction zones.
note: Highway markings are important safety devices. They show lane boundaries, indicate where passing is allowed or prohibited, guide you through intersections and interchanges, and provide warnings so you can position your vehicle correctly and drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but with no marked stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe.,b:After slowing but not stopping if no other vehicles are present.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet from the intersection whether necessary or not.
note: At a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection. After stopping, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles in all directions. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: What do two solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only when at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction, except for permitted left turns into or out of driveways or side roads.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean you must not cross them to pass another vehicle. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or when directed by law enforcement or traffic control.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A deaf person.,b:A person in a traffic study.,c:A blind person.
note: A person using a white cane or accompanied by a guide dog is usually blind or visually impaired. You must yield the right-of-way, stop well back if needed, and use extra caution, because they may not see approaching vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return immediately after passing.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Remain in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.
note: After passing on a two-lane road, do not move back too soon. Wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space to return to your lane without cutting the other driver off.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:Only the color of the vehicle.,c:The driver’s height.
note: Braking distance increases with higher speed and is affected by how well your brakes and tires work and by the road surface. Wet, icy, or gravel roads and worn brakes or tires all increase the distance needed to stop.

question: Where is it particularly important to slow down?
options: a:Only on highways.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:On narrow or winding roads
note: You must reduce speed in places where hazards are more likely, such as narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills and curves, where pedestrians are present, and in bad weather. Slowing down gives you more time and space to react.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Do not immediately apply the brakes; gradually slow and pull off the road.,b:Increase speed to reach a service area sooner.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes, because that can cause you to lose control. When the vehicle is under control and slowing, carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the \D\" represent?"
options: a:Defensive driving.,b:Dodge.,c:Decide on a safe action.
note: SIPDE is a defensive driving process: Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, Execute. The “D” stands for Decide, meaning you choose the safest action based on what you see and what you think other road users will do next.

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:Only the bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. Drivers should not crowd a motorcycle or try to share the same lane side‑by‑side, because motorcycles need space to maneuver and maintain stability.

question: What does an arrow painted in a lane indicate?
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers may optionally make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: Lane arrows painted on the pavement show what movements are allowed or required from that lane, such as turn left, turn right, or go straight. You must follow the direction of the arrow, while also obeying any traffic signals or signs that control when you can make that movement.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.,d:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.
note: At a school crossing sign, slow down, scan carefully for children, and be ready to stop. Children may enter the road unexpectedly, so you must yield to any pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk.

question: When adjusting the inside rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?
options: a:Only the road directly behind the car.,b:The entire rear window without moving your head.,c:The passengers in the backseat only.,d:Your own reflection clearly.
note: Set the inside rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window while sitting in your normal driving position, using only your eyes to scan, not your head. This gives you the widest view of traffic behind you.

question: What is true about driving while distracted?
options: a:It usually causes drivers to drive faster and more safely.,b:It usually causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,c:It is never dangerous.,d:It improves multitasking skills.
note: Driving while distracted takes your eyes, mind, or hands away from driving, which slows your reaction to hazards and greatly increases crash risk. It never makes driving safer and is always dangerous.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow and a red light allows you to:
options: a:Go straight only and wait for a solid green to turn.,b:Ignore the arrow and follow the red light.,c:Proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow and only if the intersection and crosswalk are clear.,d:Stop completely; a red light always overrides a green arrow.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, even if the circular light is red. You may proceed only in the arrow’s direction, after checking that the intersection and crosswalk are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, drivers must yield the right-of-way to:
options: a:Only vehicles that signal to turn right.,b:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians already in the intersection or crosswalk.,c:Vehicles behind them on the same turning lane.,d:Only vehicles that are speeding or using their horn.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk or already in the intersection. Turn only when there is a safe gap and the way is clear.

question: When is it appropriate to use the parking brake?
options: a:Only when stopped on a busy street.,b:Only when parking on a hill.,c:Every time you park the vehicle.
note: Use the parking brake every time you park, whether on a hill or flat ground and regardless of transmission type. This adds an extra layer of security to keep the vehicle from rolling if the primary parking mechanism fails.

question: What should you do before crossing railroad tracks to be safe?
options: a:Look and listen for trains in both directions before crossing.,b:Cross quickly if you see a train approaching.,c:Listen only if warning lights are flashing.
note: Before crossing railroad tracks, slow down, look carefully in both directions, and listen for trains, even if warning lights or gates are not active. Only proceed when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to fully clear the tracks.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down a little while staying in your lane.,c:Turn on hazard lights and continue driving.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection faster.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and/or flashing lights, you must pull as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stop, allowing it a clear path to pass. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has gone by.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady green light, what should you do?
options: a:Continue driving while yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Stop even if the light is green.,c:Treat it as a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe, but you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection. Approach at a speed that allows you to stop safely if the light changes.

question: What is the result of consuming alcohol while taking drugs?
options: a:It helps relieve your illness faster.,b:It can increase the effects of both the drugs and the alcohol.,c:It decreases the effects of the drugs and alcohol.
note: Mixing alcohol with many prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal drugs usually increases the effects of both substances. This can greatly reduce coordination, judgment, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous and increasing the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:Only when they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection.,b:When entering the street from a garage,c:Only when your signal is red.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway, garage, or alley, you must yield to all traffic already on the road and to pedestrians on the sidewalk. Vehicles already on the roadway have the right-of-way because you are entering from a private area.

question: Which of the following best describes a defensive driver?
options: a:Easily distracted.,b:Anticipation of potential hazards and actions to avoid them.,c:Passivity toward traffic conditions.
note: A defensive driver constantly scans the road, anticipates what other drivers or pedestrians might do, and adjusts speed and position to avoid trouble. This includes keeping safe following distances, being prepared for sudden stops, and having an escape plan.

question: What should you do when approaching an accident scene while driving?
options: a:Drive slowly and block the scene for onlookers.,b:Stop to look at the scene.,c:Keep moving unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.
note: At an accident scene, unnecessary stopping or slowing can cause additional crashes and traffic jams. Unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely assist, continue driving, stay focused on the road, and follow directions from emergency personnel.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should remain on?
options: a:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,b:Use only parking lights without flashers.,c:Use your emergency flashers and appropriate low‑beam or parking lights so your vehicle is clearly visible.
note: If you must stop along the road at night, you want other drivers to see you clearly and in time to avoid you. Turn on your emergency flashers and, where legal and appropriate, use your low‑beam headlights or parking lights so your vehicle is visible without blinding approaching drivers. Never sit on a dark roadside with all lights off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway you should generally:
options: a:Proceed slowly on the ramp and merge at a lower speed.,b:Turn on your hazard lights while merging.,c:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of traffic and merge smoothly.
note: Freeway on‑ramps are designed as acceleration lanes so you can reach the speed of traffic before merging. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, match the speed of vehicles on the freeway when safe, and then merge smoothly, yielding to traffic already on the freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn across the median.,c:Stop and back up to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, keep driving to the next exit. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to stop on the freeway, back up, or make a U‑turn across the median. Exit safely at the next opportunity and then re-route to your destination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you expect when approaching a heavy truck while driving uphill from behind?
options: a:You should always attempt to pass quickly.,b:The truck may be moving slower than the posted speed limit.,c:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on upgrades because of their weight and engine limits, so you should expect them to be traveling below the posted speed limit when going uphill. Be prepared to adjust your speed and only pass if it is legal, safe, and you have enough clear distance and visibility.

question: What should you do if an aggressive driver is behind you?
options: a:Make every effort to get out of the aggressive driver's way and avoid eye contact.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass to warn them.,c:Speed up to challenge them.,d:Brake suddenly to show displeasure.
note: If an aggressive driver is behind you, the safest response is to avoid any confrontation. Make every safe effort to move out of their way, do not make eye contact or gestures, and do not speed up or brake suddenly to “teach them a lesson.” Your goal is to create space and let them go by.

question: Which action helps reduce the chance of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,b:Flash your lights to warn drivers behind you.,c:Brake suddenly to alert following drivers.,d:Release the accelerator to let the vehicle slow.
note: To reduce the chance of a rear‑end collision, start slowing early and smoothly so drivers behind you have time to react. First, gently release the accelerator so your vehicle begins to slow, then apply steady brake pressure. This keeps your stop predictable and your brake lights give clear warning to following drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When meeting an oncoming vehicle on a narrow road, you must:
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Demand the other driver pull over entirely.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop regardless of road width.
note: On narrow two‑way roads, each driver must share the roadway so that both vehicles can pass safely. You are required to allow the oncoming vehicle at least one‑half of the main‑traveled portion of the roadway, rather than forcing the other driver completely off the road.

question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing where there is no traffic signal?
options: a:Whoever started moving last must yield.,b:The pedestrian must yield to the turning driver.,c:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.
note: At intersections without traffic signals, drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing, whether or not there is a painted crosswalk. The pedestrian has the right-of-way, and the turning driver must wait until the pedestrian has safely crossed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a traffic signal that's been green for a long time, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Prepare for it to change to yellow and begin slowing.,c:Stop immediately before the light.,d:Assume it will remain green and continue at current speed.
note: A green light that has been green for a long time is called a "stale" green and is likely to change soon. You should cover the brake, begin to slow slightly, and be prepared to stop safely if the light turns yellow, rather than speeding up or assuming it will stay green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb is:
options: a:Required only during the maneuver,b:Necessary only if other traffic is present.,c:Optional on multilane roads.,d:Required by law and a good driving habit.
note: The law requires that you signal for at least 100 feet before you move your vehicle to the right or left; signaling is also a good driving habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what is a required action before proceeding?
options: a:Back up slowly if necessary.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection.
note: A green light means you may go if the intersection is clear, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles still in the intersection completing their movements. Do not enter until it is safe and the way is clear.

question: How should you reduce the effects of headlight glare from oncoming traffic at night?
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Look straight ahead.,c:Look over your shoulder.
note: At night, oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the white edge line and use it as a guide, rather than looking directly at the oncoming lights.

question: What should you check regarding your tires before driving?
options: a:Only that they are not wet.,b:The tread depth and that air pressure is adequate (no flat tires).,c:Only that they appear circular.
note: Before driving, make sure your tires have enough tread and are properly inflated. Low tread reduces traction, especially in rain, and underinflated or flat tires can overheat, fail suddenly, and make steering and braking much harder.

question: What do orange traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Work zone or construction area warnings.,b:Regulatory rules such as speed limits.,c:School zone areas.,d:Hospital zones.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work or construction zones. They warn you about road work, lane shifts, workers, and equipment so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: Why should you not follow other vehicles too closely?
options: a:It reduces your fuel efficiency.,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.,d:You won't be able to see the rear lights.
note: If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or distance to react and stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you room to brake smoothly and avoid rear-end collisions.

question: Which factor greatly affects your ability to stop quickly?
options: a:The condition of the road surface.,b:The color of your vehicle.,c:The number of passengers in your car.
note: The condition of the road surface has a major impact on how quickly you can stop. Wet, icy, or loose gravel surfaces greatly reduce traction, increasing your stopping distance, so you must slow down and allow more space to stop safely.

question: When sharing the road with trucks, remember they generally:
options: a:Require longer distances to stop and more space to maneuver than smaller vehicles.,b:Require less stopping distance than passenger cars.,c:Have smaller blind spots than cars.
note: Large trucks are much heavier and need more distance to stop and more space to turn or change lanes. Give them extra room, avoid cutting in front of them, and remember they also have large blind spots where they may not see you.

question: When you hear a siren behind you while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.,b:Speed up to create space quickly.,c:Stop immediately in the middle of the lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. If traffic or road conditions make it impossible to pull over immediately, slow down, keep moving carefully, and create space as soon as you can so the emergency vehicle can get through.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no signals, you should:
options: a:Stop only if you see or hear a train approaching.,b:Assume all crossings have signals and proceed normally.,c:Slow down, look and listen, and be prepared to stop if a train is coming.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or lights, you are not required to stop every time, but you must approach with extreme caution. Slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if you cannot safely cross. Only proceed when you are sure the tracks are clear and there is enough room to fully clear the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should drivers do when approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Stop before proceeding.,b:Increase your speed to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. It warns that there may be cross traffic, pedestrians, or another hazard in or near the intersection. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety, but you must be prepared to yield and adjust your speed so you can react safely.

question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:
options: a:Making sudden stops.,b:Driving through shallow water.,c:Driving too fast for the wet road surface.
note: Hydroplaning happens when a layer of water builds up between your tires and the road so the tires lose contact with the pavement. This is most likely at higher speeds on wet roads, especially when there is standing water or worn tires. To reduce the risk, slow down in rain, avoid sudden steering or braking, and make sure your tires are in good condition.

question: When passing a parked vehicle, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:You should honk to alert them before passing.,b:A person or vehicle might unexpectedly move into your lane.,c:Pedestrians and drivers will always respect your right-of-way.
note: When passing parked vehicles, you should expect the unexpected. A door may open suddenly, a person may step out from between cars, or a vehicle may pull away from the curb without signaling. Slow slightly if needed, leave extra space when possible, and be ready to brake or steer smoothly to avoid hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously at an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver signaling first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,d:The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled (open) intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: How is defensive driving best defined?
options: a:Driving aggressively to gain position in traffic.,b:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,c:Driving against the flow of traffic if necessary.
note: Defensive driving means using safe driving strategies to reduce risk: staying alert, anticipating what other road users might do, adjusting to weather and traffic conditions, and leaving yourself space and time to react so you can avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas.,b:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,c:When driving so slowly that it disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
note: You must not drive so slowly that you block or interfere with the normal, safe flow of traffic, unless it is necessary for safety or required by law. Impeding traffic by driving far below the speed of other vehicles can be illegal and unsafe.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who disobeys traffic laws?
options: a:They are always given only a warning.,b:They are exempt from traffic laws.,c:They can be ticketed just like motor vehicle drivers.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and they can receive tickets for violations such as running red lights or stop signs.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly,b:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach your destination.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly to keep control of the vehicle, stay off the brakes at first, and gently ease your foot off the accelerator. Let the vehicle slow down gradually, then carefully steer to the side of the road and brake lightly once you are under control and out of traffic.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Rely solely on your side mirrors.,b:Only check the rearview mirror.,c:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you intend to move.
note: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, first use your mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move. This over-the-shoulder check lets you see areas your mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles hidden in your blind spot.

question: When preparing to change lanes, what minimum-sized gap should you look for?
options: a:Only a half-second gap.,b:Four- or five-second gap in the lane you want to enter.,c:Two-second gap.,d:One-second gap.
note: Before changing lanes, you should look for a gap of about four to five seconds in the lane you want to enter. This larger time gap gives you enough space to signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and move over smoothly without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes go the same direction and passing is allowed.,b:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is prohibited for both directions.,c:You may pass if you are careful.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only when turning left into or out of a driveway or side road, when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop.,b:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,c:Ignore signs if there are no gates.,d:Proceed unless you hear a horn.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If red lights are flashing, gates are down, or a train is clearly approaching, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until it is safe to proceed.

question: Signs that warn of hazardous conditions ahead are classified as:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Warning signs.
note: Warning signs alert you to hazardous or changing conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings. They give you time to slow down or adjust your driving so you can respond safely to the upcoming situation.

question: Why is it important to leave a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It prevents all distractions from other vehicles.,b:It keeps traffic flowing evenly.,c:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
note: Leaving a space cushion around your vehicle gives you time and room to react if another driver suddenly stops, swerves, or if a hazard appears. This extra space helps you brake smoothly or steer around problems instead of making sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

question: What does a red arrow displayed on a traffic signal require of drivers?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or a green arrow appears.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped in the lane controlled by that arrow. You cannot make the movement indicated by the arrow until a green arrow or green light appears and it is safe to proceed.

question: When in a line of traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:Make sure there is enough space ahead so your vehicle can fully clear the tracks without stopping.,c:Always stop halfway on the tracks to check for trains.,d:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
note: When traffic is moving slowly over railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle before you start across. This prevents you from being trapped on the tracks if traffic stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do your vehicle's brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:You are making a turn.,b:You are changing lanes.,c:You have the emergency brake engaged.,d:You are slowing down or stopping.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. Keeping them in good working order gives others time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign warn you about?
options: a:Public recreation areas.,b:School zones.,c:Existing or possible road hazards.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert you to existing or possible hazards on or near the roadway, such as curves, intersections, or road work, so you can adjust your driving in advance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit or turn on a freeway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop and back up on the freeway shoulder.,b:Make an immediate turn from your current lane.,c:Continue to the next exit or safe location to turn around.
note: If you miss your exit or turn on a freeway, keep going to the next exit or other safe place to turn around. Never stop, back up on the shoulder, or make a sudden turn across lanes, because those actions can cause serious rear‑end or side‑impact crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multilane road when you see a 'Merging traffic' sign, how should you respond?
options: a:Always maintain your present speed even if someone is trying to merge.,b:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,c:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes if safe.
note: When you see a merging traffic sign, be prepared for vehicles entering your lane. If it is safe, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed slightly to create a gap. Do not speed up to block them or honk unnecessarily; smooth merging keeps traffic flowing and reduces collisions.

question: If you are in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move left, what steps should you take?
options: a:Turn on your headlights and then move.,b:Only look into your rearview mirror before moving.,c:Check mirrors, blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before moving left on a multilane highway, check your rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and signal your lane change. Only move when you are sure the lane is clear and you have enough space; this sequence helps prevent collisions with vehicles you may not see in your mirrors alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:Slow speeds.,b:High speeds.,c:Night driving.
note: Higher speeds mean it takes much longer to stop and crashes are far more severe. As speed increases, both stopping distance and the force of impact increase dramatically, so driving too fast for conditions greatly raises your risk of a serious collision.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph require to stop?
options: a:About 50 feet.,b:About 125 feet.,c:About 400 feet.,d:About 200 feet.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. A fully loaded tractor‑trailer traveling about 55 mph can need roughly 400 feet—more than the length of a football field—to come to a complete stop, so you should avoid cutting closely in front of them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a public road from a private driveway or private road?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching cars.,c:Pull partway onto the road and stop to alert drivers.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Wait until traffic is clear and it is safe before pulling out; drivers on the public road have the right-of-way.

question: If there's an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, how should you handle passing?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder to pass both at once.,b:Try to split the difference and squeeze between both hazards.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When you face hazards on both sides—like an oncoming car on the left and a bicyclist on the right—do not try to squeeze between them. Let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then move over and pass the bicyclist only when you can give them plenty of space and it is safe.

question: When traffic signals are horizontal, where is the yellow light located?
options: a:On the right.,b:On the left.,c:In the middle.
note: On standard horizontal traffic signals, the yellow (amber) light is in the center, with red on the left and green on the right. The yellow light warns that the signal is about to change to red and you should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:A requirement to stop fully.,b:Proceed with caution.,c:Pedestrian-only crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down and proceed with caution. Be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that may be entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill next to a curb, which way should you turn your steering wheel?
options: a:Turn the wheel toward the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Leave the wheel straight and do not use parking brake.,c:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,d:Turn the wheel away from the curb and set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move toward the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How can drivers prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stop regularly to rest and stretch.,b:Slow down and drive more cautiously.,c:Turn up the radio volume continuously.
note: Scheduling regular breaks to rest and stretch reduces drowsiness and helps drivers stay alert on long journeys.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the definition of a speed limit?
options: a:The suggested speed under dangerous conditions.,b:The required speed during rain.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A speed limit is the maximum (and sometimes minimum, where posted) legal speed allowed under ideal conditions. Drivers must reduce speed below the limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: If you're angry after a work incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to mask your emotions while driving.,b:Take a few minutes to calm down before getting behind the wheel.,c:Drive fast on the highway to blow off steam.
note: If you are angry or very upset, you should wait and take a few minutes to calm down before driving. Strong emotions can reduce your concentration, slow your reaction time, and lead to aggressive or risky decisions behind the wheel.

question: Which safety restraint combination provides the most protection in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Only a lap belt.,c:Only an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together. Seat belts keep you properly positioned and prevent ejection, while airbags provide extra cushioning in certain types of collisions. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the I stand for?
options: a:Identify hazards.,b:Ignore distractions.,c:Increase speed.
note: In the SIPDE process, the I stands for Identify. After you scan the road, you identify specific hazards such as other vehicles, pedestrians, road signs, and changing conditions so you can decide how to respond safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, what is the proper way to merge into traffic?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.,b:Use only your mirrors and immediately merge at any speed.,c:Use the acceleration lane to match the freeway traffic speed and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.,d:Signal and enter without checking blind spots.
note: On a freeway entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic on the freeway. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge when there is a safe gap, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: What should you remember about wet pavement and rainfall?
options: a:Pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:Wet roads never cause hydroplaning.,c:You do not need extra space when stopping on wet pavement.
note: When it first starts to rain, water mixes with oil and other residue on the road, making the surface especially slippery. Slow down, increase following distance, and be alert for reduced traction and possible hydroplaning on wet pavement.

question: Which medications can impair your driving ability?
options: a:Only diet pills.,b:Only over-the-counter cold medicine.,c:Any medication.,d:Only prescription painkillers.
note: Any medication—prescription, over‑the‑counter, or herbal—can impair driving by causing drowsiness, blurred vision, slowed reaction time, or other side effects. Always read labels and ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it is safe to drive after taking a medication.

question: Your risk of being killed is how many times greater if you are thrown from a vehicle in a crash?
options: a:20 times.,b:25 times.,c:10 times.
note: Being ejected from a vehicle in a crash makes you far more likely to be killed—about 25 times more likely than if you remain inside and restrained. Wearing a seat belt keeps you inside the vehicle and greatly reduces your risk of death or serious injury.

question: When making a turn, what should you look at?
options: a:Look as far ahead around the bend as possible in the direction you want to go.,b:Watch only the cars behind you.,c:Look only at vegetation that blocks your view.,d:Focus solely on the curb.
note: When turning, look well ahead through the turn in the direction you want to go, not just directly in front of your vehicle. Looking far ahead helps you steer smoothly, judge your path, and react early to hazards.

question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:After you start passing.,c:Only if the vehicle you are passing signals.,d:Early enough that other drivers understand your intention before you begin the maneuver.
note: You should always signal well before you start to pass so other drivers have time to see and understand what you plan to do. Signaling only at the last moment does not give others enough time to react safely.

question: Which is a good habit of a defensive driver?
options: a:Traveling at a constant speed regardless of conditions.,b:Watching for the actions of other drivers and anticipating hazards.,c:Always driving slowly no matter the conditions.
note: A defensive driver stays alert, watches what other drivers are doing, and anticipates possible hazards so they can react early and safely. Driving slowly all the time is not automatically defensive; you must adjust your speed and actions to current traffic, road, and weather conditions.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.
note: Mixing alcohol with other drugs often increases the effects of both, leading to much greater impairment than either substance alone. This can severely reduce judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, you should allow a larger space cushion:
options: a:At a stop sign only.,b:In front of your vehicle.,c:At intersections only.
note: When stopped facing uphill, leave extra space in front of your vehicle. If the vehicle behind you rolls backward when starting, the added space in front gives you room to move forward slightly and avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in a lane marked for turning but you want to go straight, what should you do?
options: a:Reverse your vehicle and merge back into traffic.,b:Put on your signal and wait to merge into through-traffic.,c:Complete the turn as required by the lane.
note: If you are already in a turn-only lane, you must follow the lane’s direction and complete the turn. Other drivers are expecting you to turn, and going straight from a turn-only lane can cause crashes. After the turn, find a safe way to return to your intended route.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the signal, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to warn them and continue.,b:Proceed as usual because you have the right-of-way.,c:Speed up to pass in front of them.,d:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely.
note: Even if you have a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk, even if they are crossing against the signal. Stop and allow them to cross safely, then proceed when the crosswalk is clear.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash generally mean?
options: a:The indicated action is prohibited.,b:Drivers must come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown is not allowed. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red slash means no right turn at that location.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what steps must you take?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Turn off the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Continue through at the same speed you were traveling.,c:Stop and wait for a green light.
note: A flashing yellow signal means proceed with caution. You do not stop like a red light; instead, slow down, scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down after you enter the exit ramp, not before.,b:Slow down before entering the ramp.,c:Keep your speed constant throughout the ramp.
note: On a freeway, maintain your speed in the through lane until you are in the exit ramp’s deceleration lane. Once you are fully in the ramp, then reduce speed to match the posted ramp speed and roadway conditions.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,b:Work hard to steer, reduce speed, and pull off to a safe location to stop.,c:Honk repeatedly and turn off the ignition immediately.
note: If power steering fails, the vehicle will still steer, but it will take much more physical effort. Hold the wheel firmly, slow down smoothly, and carefully steer to the side of the road where you can stop safely. Do not turn off the ignition while moving, because that can lock the steering wheel.

question: What is the best way to deal with a driver who is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to teach them a lesson.,b:Brake-check them.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.,d:Speed up to increase the distance between you.
note: When another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to create space, not to confront them. Maintain a steady speed, then change lanes when safe or gradually slow down to encourage the tailgater to pass. Never slam on your brakes or brake-check, as this can cause a rear-end collision and is considered aggressive driving.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, you should:
options: a:Cross immediately because only one train can pass at a time.,b:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks before proceeding.,c:Proceed as soon as one train passes.
note: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, a second train can come from either direction after the first one passes. Stay stopped until all warning devices stop, the gate (if any) is fully up, and you have a clear view down every track in both directions. Only then proceed across the tracks.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is correct?
options: a:It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.,b:A motorcycle with two people is more stable than one with a single rider.,c:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full traffic lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and pass as you would a car. Do not share the lane or crowd the motorcycle, and avoid following too closely because motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles.

question: If an emergency vehicle using lights or siren approaches you on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Speed up and leave the street as fast as possible.,b:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,c:Drive with your hazard lights on.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, you must pull toward the nearest edge or curb—right or left—clear of any intersection, and stop until it has passed. Do not speed up or continue driving with hazard lights on; the goal is to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection with functioning signals, whose directions must you follow?
options: a:The traffic light's indications.,b:The officer's directions.,c:Whichever is more convenient.
note: When a police officer is directing traffic, you must follow the officer’s hand signals and commands, even if they conflict with traffic lights or signs. The officer’s directions temporarily override normal traffic controls to keep traffic flowing safely.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Tell the owner you are unsure and drive without learning the controls.,b:Assume everything works the same and drive immediately.,c:Familiarize yourself with the controls (lights, wipers, signals, gear selector, and mirrors) and check for obvious safety issues before driving.
note: Before driving a vehicle you do not know well, you should first learn where and how to operate the essential controls—such as lights, wipers, turn signals, gear selector, parking brake, and hazard flashers—and make sure there are no obvious safety problems. Being familiar with the controls helps you respond quickly and safely in traffic.

question: Which action best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check behind the vehicle before you get in and back up.,b:Rely only on rearview mirrors while inside the vehicle.,c:Sound your horn just before shifting into reverse.
note: Before backing, walk around and look behind your vehicle to check for children, pedestrians, and obstacles that may be too low to see from the driver’s seat. Once inside, back up slowly and continue to check all mirrors and over your shoulder. Never rely only on mirrors, cameras, or sensors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, what steps should you take?
options: a:Signal your lane change.,b:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,c:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,d:All of the above.
note: A safe lane change requires several steps together: first check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, then glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and signal to let others know your intention. Make the lane change only when it is safe and maintain a steady speed.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more at night.,b:It is more likely to be raining at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: At night, your ability to see is reduced because headlights only illuminate a limited distance and it is harder to see pedestrians, animals, and road hazards. You should use your headlights correctly, reduce your speed so you can stop within the distance you can see, and increase your following distance.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing permitted from the lane next to the solid line.,b:No passing permitted in either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line only.,d:Passing permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and not allowed for traffic on the side with the solid line. The broken-line side may cross the center line to pass when it is safe and legal; the solid-line side must stay in its lane.

question: When making a turn, what should you do with your speed?
options: a:Vary your speed unpredictably.,b:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow to a safe speed so you can maintain control, stay in your lane, and react to hazards. Enter the turn at a reduced speed, then gently accelerate as you exit if conditions allow.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).,b:Turn your wheels to the left (away from the curb).,c:Keep the wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two-way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, the front tire will rest against the curb and the car will move away from traffic instead of into the roadway.

question: When is it appropriate to begin accelerating during a turn?
options: a:Immediately after you start the turn.,b:Before you begin the turn.,c:Only after you reach the halfway point in the bend.,d:Begin accelerating near the middle of the curve after you have established your path.
note: For safe cornering, slow before the turn, then maintain a steady speed as you begin turning. Once you are in the middle of the curve, your path is stable, and you can see through the turn, you may begin to gently accelerate to exit smoothly.

question: If an oncoming car has blinding headlights, you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.,b:Use your high beams so you can see better.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road until it passes.
note: When an oncoming vehicle’s headlights are blinding, do not look directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road and use it as a guide until the vehicle passes, helping preserve your night vision and lane position.

question: What do solid white stop lines painted across lanes indicate?
options: a:They indicate church and school zones.,b:They mark no-parking areas.,c:They are painted only in curves and on hills.,d:Stop lines mark the exact location to stop at intersections and crosswalks.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at intersections and crosswalks. They show you exactly where to stop so you are behind the crosswalk or intersection and not blocking pedestrians or cross traffic.

question: Which statement about driving in changing weather is true?
options: a:A sudden change in weather requires adjusting your driving (e.g., slow down in rain or fog).,b:You should always maintain the same speed regardless of weather.,c:Be less aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.,d:Turn on cruise control in rain.
note: When weather changes—such as rain, fog, snow, or ice—you must adjust your driving. Typically you slow down, increase following distance, and use appropriate lights so you have enough time and space to react to reduced visibility and traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what is that hand signal indicating?
options: a:The driver plans to turn right.,b:The driver plans to turn left.,c:The driver plans to stop or slow down.
note: Standard hand signals in the U.S. are: left arm straight out for a left turn, left arm bent upward for a right turn, and left arm extended downward for slowing or stopping. If you see a driver’s left arm pointing down, be prepared for them to slow or stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a stop sign, how should you scan before proceeding?
options: a:Move as soon as the vehicle ahead moves.,b:Only check behind you for tailgaters.,c:Look left first, then right, and left again before proceeding.
note: At a stop sign, come to a complete stop, then scan carefully: look left first because traffic from the left is usually closer, then look right, and then left again before proceeding. This pattern helps you spot vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists that may be entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires drivers to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Merge to the right immediately.,c:Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any pedestrians and cross traffic, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

question: An emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches from behind. What must you do?
options: a:Continue driving and try to stay out of its way.,b:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop when safe.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights (and usually a siren) approaches from behind, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, continue through it first, then pull over. Never speed up or try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slants toward the left, what does that indicate?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:An intersection is just ahead.,c:The road will narrow ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the travel lane. When this line slants or angles toward the center of the road, it means the usable roadway is narrowing and your lane is getting smaller. You should be prepared to adjust your position and speed to stay safely within the lane.

question: Which of the following actions can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Talking on the phone, eating, or looking at reading material.,b:Eating,c:Only looking at reading material occasionally.
note: Distracted driving is caused by any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Eating, using a phone, reading, adjusting controls, or interacting with passengers can all be distractions and increase your crash risk. Safe drivers avoid any non‑driving tasks while the vehicle is moving.

question: Which behavior may indicate a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving slightly slower than traffic.,b:Weaving between lanes.,c:Maintaining a constant speed.
note: Weaving between lanes, drifting across lane markings, sudden swerving, and other erratic movements are common signs of an impaired driver. Alcohol and drugs affect coordination and judgment, making it hard to maintain a steady lane position. If you see this behavior, stay back and report it when safe.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgement.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgement.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and body functions. It harms both judgment and driving skills by reducing reaction time, coordination, vision, and the ability to make safe decisions. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect your driving and increase the chance of a crash.

question: When should you use one-hand steering?
options: a:At all times when driving in town.,b:For high-speed maneuvers to increase control.,c:When avoiding hazards at high speed.,d:Only when backing or operating controls that require a brief reach.
note: Use one-hand steering only for backing or when briefly reaching to operate controls such as wipers or headlights.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
