options: a:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.,b:When exiting an expressway.,c:When following a motorcycle.,d:In any situation where visibility or stopping distance is reduced, such as behind large vehicles, in bad weather, heavy traffic, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.
note: Increase your following distance any time conditions make it harder to see or stop safely. This includes when you are behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when following motorcycles or bicycles, and when someone is tailgating you. More space gives you extra time to react and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always use a turn signal?
options: a:When pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:When changing lanes.,c:When pulling into or out of a parking space.,d:Whenever you turn, change lanes, or move into or out of traffic, including from alleys, driveways, or parking spaces.
note: You must always use your turn signal any time you intend to turn, change lanes, or move your vehicle laterally or into traffic so others know what you plan to do. This includes changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, and entering traffic from an alley, driveway, or parking area. Signaling early and clearly helps prevent crashes by giving other drivers time to adjust.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular signs usually indicate?
options: a:Construction ahead.,b:Yield — slow and give right-of-way when necessary.,c:No U-turn.,d:School zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for a yield sign. At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop, giving the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe and does not interfere with others.

question: If an intersection's traffic signals are out because of a power outage, you should treat it as:
options: a:A location to park and wait for power to be restored.,b:A four-way stop—stop and proceed when it's your turn.,c:A place to turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
note: If traffic signals are completely out at an intersection, treat it as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, then proceed in the order of arrival, yielding to any vehicle already in the intersection and to the right if you arrive at the same time. This helps keep traffic moving safely when signals are not working.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:The area directly behind your vehicle only.,b:An area you cannot see without turning your head.,c:The view you have in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see by using your mirrors alone. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
options: a:It means the same as a green light.,b:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in that direction.,c:Drivers may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic.,d:It is only advisory and may be ignored if clear.
note: A solid red arrow means you must come to a complete stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction of the arrow while it is red. It has the same legal force as a circular red light for that specific direction.

question: What is a good practice to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Drive continuously and keep caffeine levels high.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time to stay alert.,c:Do arm exercises while driving.,d:Stop and rest approximately every two hours.
note: On long trips, fatigue reduces your alertness and reaction time. A good practice is to stop about every two hours to get out, stretch, and rest briefly so you stay alert and safe behind the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single broken yellow centerline indicate on a two-lane road?
options: a:Traffic must stay in the right lane at all times.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so, but you must return to your lane before oncoming traffic gets close.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do on a two-lane or undivided highway?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,b:Slow down and keep moving at a reduced speed.,c:Stop immediately in the lane where you are driving.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches on a two-lane or undivided highway, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as is safe and come to a stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

question: If another vehicle seems likely to hit you, what is the appropriate action to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Use your emergency lights.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to warn another driver or pedestrian if they may not see you and a collision could occur. The horn is the standard, legal way to get another road user’s attention quickly in an emergency.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, which part of the road should you look toward?
options: a:The oncoming vehicle's headlights.,b:The center of the road.,c:Either side.,d:The right side of the road.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide. This reduces glare from the other headlights while helping you stay in your lane.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes when driving on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,b:Get off highways as quickly as possible.,c:Add extra weight to improve traction.,d:Use cruise control to maintain speed.
note: On snow or ice, slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Extra following distance gives you time to brake gently and avoid skids; cruise control should not be used on slippery roads.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color line?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:Red lines.,c:White lines.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, helping drivers know where passing is allowed and where it is not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must traffic signs and pavement markings be treated by drivers?
options: a:Follow them only at night.,b:They must always be obeyed.,c:Only obey them when other vehicles are present.,d:They are optional suggestions.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that all drivers must obey at all times, not just when other vehicles are around or only at night. Ignoring them is both unsafe and illegal.

question: What is a likely effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:It makes you a better driver because you are less hungry.,b:It causes no driving errors.,c:It distracts you and makes staying in your lane and controlling the vehicle more difficult.
note: Eating or drinking while driving takes at least one hand off the wheel and your attention off the road. This makes it harder to keep a steady lane position, react quickly to hazards, and maintain full control of the vehicle.

question: How do blind spots compare on larger vehicles versus smaller?
options: a:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,b:Blind spots are the same regardless of vehicle size.,c:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,d:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks and buses sit higher and have more body length and width, which creates bigger areas around the vehicle that the driver cannot see in mirrors. These larger blind spots make it easier for smaller vehicles or pedestrians to be hidden from the driver’s view.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Flash your lights to warn them.,b:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.,d:Honk continuously to hurry them.
note: Drivers must slow down and be prepared to stop for pedestrians crossing the road and must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. Flashing lights, honking, or speeding up can confuse or endanger the pedestrian; the safe and legal action is to yield and allow them to cross safely.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. Under which conditions must you still stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted,b:If a crossing gate is lowered.,c:If lights are flashing.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing whenever a stop sign is posted, even if you do not see or hear a train. You also must stop if gates are down, warning lights are flashing, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is approaching and could be a hazard. Always obey posted signs and active warning devices at railroad crossings.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,b:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.,c:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.
note: Driving too fast for conditions—such as rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road surfaces—reduces the time you have to react and increases stopping distance. Even if you are below the posted speed limit, you can still be driving too fast for current conditions and increase your risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate to avoid a red light.,b:Continue as you have the right-of-way.,c:Slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection; do not stop in the middle.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green arrow before moving.,b:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and yield to pedestrians and other vehicles as required.,c:Always speed up to get through before the light changes.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, but only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. You must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to oncoming traffic when turning left, and obey any signs that restrict turns.

question: When turning left, on which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A solid green circular light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A green arrow pointing left.
note: A green left arrow is a protected turn signal. When it is lit, oncoming traffic facing a red light must stop, and you have the right-of-way to make the left turn, after checking that the intersection is clear. A solid green or flashing yellow does not give you automatic right-of-way; you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Turn on cruise control in wet conditions.,b:Speed up to pass standing water quickly.,c:Use tires with proper air pressure and good tread.,d:Drive with your parking lights on.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. You reduce this risk by keeping your tires properly inflated, making sure they have good tread, and slowing down on wet roads, especially in heavy rain or standing water. Avoid sudden steering or braking in these conditions.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams to warn them.,b:Follow and confront them at the next stop.,c:Let it go and continue driving safely.,d:Pull alongside and yell at the driver.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and avoid any aggressive response. Do not chase, confront, or try to punish the other driver. Instead, slow slightly if needed to create space, maintain a safe following distance, and continue driving defensively. This helps prevent road rage and reduces the chance of a collision.

question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Wait until a traffic signal or stop sign before passing.,b:Sound your horn and pass closely.,c:Pass with at least three feet of clearance after ensuring no oncoming traffic.,d:Speed up and pass quickly in the same lane.
note: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, treat a bicycle like a slow-moving vehicle. Wait until the oncoming lane is clear, then move over and pass only when it is safe, leaving at least three feet of space (or more if possible). Never squeeze by in the same lane or pass too closely.

question: Under normal driving conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:One second.
note: Under normal conditions, you should use at least a three‑second following distance. Pick a fixed object ahead; when the vehicle in front passes it, start counting. If you reach the object before three seconds, you are following too closely. Increase this gap in bad weather, at higher speeds, or when visibility is reduced.

question: Which of the following is an effect of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:No effect if you feel sober.,b:Loss of concentration,c:Improved night vision.,d:Increased alertness and faster reflexes.
note: Alcohol affects driving even if you feel sober. It slows your reflexes, reduces concentration, harms judgment, and affects vision and coordination. Because of this, any amount of alcohol can make you an unsafe driver.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to lower your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limit driving to weekdays.,b:Drive only during daylight.,c:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,d:Wear your seat belt.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to control the vehicle.

question: Which takes precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A steady red light.,c:Directions from a police officer or authorized traffic control person.
note: Directions from a police officer or other authorized traffic control person always override traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings. If an officer or flagger tells you to do something different from what the signal or sign indicates, you must follow their instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers may not pass from either direction where the centerline is:
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow.,b:Double solid yellow.,c:Single broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow line in the center of a two‑way road means vehicles traveling in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You may cross only when making a permitted left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, but not to overtake and pass another vehicle.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, you should:
options: a:Turn the wheel away from the direction of the skid.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,c:Overcorrect and steer sharply.
note: When your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding). This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain traction. Avoid overcorrecting or jerking the wheel, which can make the skid worse.

question: What practice helps you avoid emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Stay only in the right lane regardless of speed.,b:Honk frequently to make others aware of you.,c:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.
note: Looking well ahead and keeping a safe following distance gives you time to see slowing or stopped traffic early and brake smoothly. This reduces the need for sudden emergency stops and lowers the risk of rear‑end collisions.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light is about to appear?
options: a:Steady green.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady red.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before the intersection. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Stop.,b:Hospital.,c:Speed limit.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is used exclusively for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When should drivers use hand-over-hand steering?
options: a:When turning at low speeds such as at intersections or parking.,b:For high-speed evasive maneuvers.,c:Only when driving straight.
note: Hand‑over‑hand steering is used for low‑speed, tight turns such as at intersections, driveways, and parking maneuvers. At higher speeds, smoother steering methods like push‑pull are safer and provide better control.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the 'E' stand for?
options: a:Elaborate on decisions.,b:Execute a maneuver.,c:Exhaust the brakes.
note: SIPDE stands for Search, Identify, Predict, Decide, Execute. After you decide how to respond to a hazard, you must execute that decision by taking action, such as braking, steering, or accelerating.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning right on a green light, you must:
options: a:Maintain your normal driving speed.,b:Yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.,c:Stop and check for nearby police vehicles before turning.
note: A green light allows you to proceed, but it does not give you the right to ignore others. When turning right on green, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or entering the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: When you approach an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, you must:
options: a:Stop immediately in your lane.,b:Drive past without changing speed.,c:Slow down and, if safe, move over to a lane farther from the stopped vehicle.
note: If an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, change lanes away if safe; otherwise slow below the posted limit and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best action when a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection?
options: a:Brake sharply to stop immediately.,b:Speed up to try to beat the red light.,c:Be prepared to stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop before the intersection if you can do so safely, rather than speeding up or braking so hard that you lose control.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:You travel faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicyclist.
note: When passing a bicyclist, you must be especially careful because you will be moving into or toward the oncoming lane. Oncoming drivers may not expect you to pull out to pass, and the bicyclist may need to swerve to avoid potholes or debris. Always check for oncoming traffic, give the bicyclist plenty of space, and only pass when you can do so safely without surprising other road users.

question: Who must use a safety belt in Louisiana?
options: a:All occupants of the vehicle (driver and passengers).,b:Only the driver.,c:Only passengers in the front seat.,d:Only passengers under 18.
note: Louisiana law requires every occupant in a motor vehicle, both driver and passengers in all seating positions, to use a safety belt or appropriate child restraint. Wearing seat belts greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash, so everyone in the vehicle must be properly buckled.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which traffic control?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A steady red light.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must treat the intersection like it is controlled by a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to go.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck (no gates or flashing lights), what should you do?
options: a:Enter the crossing and trust other drivers to warn you.,b:Turn your radio down and cross quickly.,c:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,d:Speed up to beat any possible train.
note: At a railroad crossing that has only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you must approach very carefully. Slow down, look and listen in both directions for trains, and be prepared to stop. Cross the tracks only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely without stopping on them.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate once the bus door closes.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road and proceed with caution.,c:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
note: After stopping for a school bus with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Even then, proceed slowly and watch carefully for children who may still be walking near or across the road. Children can be unpredictable, so continue at a reduced speed and be ready to stop again if needed.

question: Red pavement markings or reflectors indicate what?
options: a:A designated passing zone.,b:A temporary slowdown area.,c:Increased speed limits ahead.,d:A roadway or lane that must not be entered (no entry).
note: Red pavement markings or reflectors are used to indicate areas where traffic must not enter or travel, such as the wrong side of a divided highway or exit ramp. If you see red reflectors facing you, you are going the wrong way and must turn around immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good practice when driving to an area you are not familiar with?
options: a:Plan your route in advance.,b:Drive with only a general idea of your destination.,c:Rely only on road signs to find your way.
note: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should plan your route in advance so you can focus on the road and traffic instead of searching for directions while driving. Reviewing maps or GPS before you leave reduces last‑minute lane changes and distractions, which helps you drive more safely.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident, what should you do?
options: a:Move the vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.,b:Never move the vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Wait for police before moving it.
note: If you are involved in a minor crash and your vehicle is blocking traffic, you should move it off the traveled portion of the roadway if it is safe and possible to do so. This helps prevent additional collisions. You must still stop at or near the scene, exchange information, and provide any necessary aid before leaving.

question: When driving in rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, you should use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road and be seen by others. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or mist and make it harder for you and other drivers to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down for a highway exit?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:Before you reach the exit lane on the main highway.,c:Only once you see the toll booth.
note: You should maintain highway speed on the main lanes and move into the exit lane first, then begin slowing down once you are in that lane. Slowing on the main highway before entering the exit lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: Which springtime driving hazard is mentioned?
options: a:Longer daylight hours only.,b:Improved traction everywhere.,c:Increased potholes.
note: Spring often brings more potholes because winter freezing and thawing damage the road surface. Drivers should watch for potholes, which can damage tires and suspension or cause loss of control, especially at higher speeds or in wet conditions.

question: A curb painted which color indicates handicap parking restriction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Blue.
note: Blue painted curbs or markings typically indicate parking reserved for persons with disabilities. Only vehicles displaying valid disabled placards or license plates may park there, and misuse can result in fines and towing.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You may always drive around lowered gates if no train appears.,b:It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates,c:All crossings have flashing red signals and gates.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates, even if you do not see a train. Always stop when gates are down or lights are flashing, and proceed only when the signals indicate it is safe and the tracks are clear.

question: Under what condition may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:At any time of day.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:When it is safe to change lanes or pass.
note: A dashed (broken) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it when you are changing lanes or passing, but only after checking mirrors and blind spots and making sure it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard immediately.,b:Try to steer straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas.,c:Maintain speed and steer as usual.
note: When a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, and gradually slow down by easing off the accelerator. Avoid hard braking until the vehicle is under control, then steer to a safe place off the road and stop.

question: Which trait is characteristic of a defensive driver?
options: a:Anger.,b:Good judgment.,c:Passivity.
note: Defensive drivers stay calm, use good judgment, and anticipate hazards so they can react early and avoid collisions. Anger leads to aggressive driving and poor decisions, while passivity can mean failing to respond when needed. Using sound judgment to adjust speed, following distance, and lane position is a key trait of defensive driving.

question: Which is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Speed up before entering the curve and slow down when exiting.,b:Maintain exactly the same speed through the entire curve.,c:Slow down as you enter the curve and increase speed gradually as you exit.
note: Before a curve, you should slow down to a safe speed while the vehicle is still straight, then gently accelerate as you exit the curve. This helps maintain traction and control. Entering too fast or braking hard in the middle of the curve can cause skidding or loss of control.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using lights or siren, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get out of its way.,b:Stop immediately.,c:Continue to drive normally.
note: You are required to yield and clear a path only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without lights or siren, treat it like any other vehicle and continue driving normally, following all traffic laws and not impeding traffic.

question: Why should you adjust your headrest before driving?
options: a:They increase your seating comfort.,b:They improve rear visibility.,c:Headrests help prevent whiplash in a collision.
note: Head restraints are a safety device designed to reduce whiplash injuries in rear-end collisions. Adjust the headrest so the top is roughly level with the top of your head and close to the back of your head. Proper adjustment helps support your head and neck if your vehicle is struck from behind.

question: If you drink alcohol socially, what helps ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Arrange a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Take a cold shower before driving.,c:Exercise to sober up.,d:Drink coffee before driving.
note: The only safe choice after drinking is not to drive at all. Arrange a ride with a sober friend, use a taxi or rideshare, or stay where you are until you are sober. Coffee, cold showers, and exercise do not reduce your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

question: What should you do first when it starts to rain while you are driving?
options: a:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through quickly.,b:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,c:Keep driving at the posted maximum speed regardless of conditions.
note: When rain starts, the road becomes slippery, especially in the first few minutes as oil and dirt mix with water. You should immediately slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see and be seen. If visibility becomes very poor or conditions feel unsafe, pull over safely and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Ignore it if no cars are visible.,b:Always come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must yield the right‑of‑way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. If there is no traffic or pedestrians, you may proceed without stopping, but at a safe, controlled speed.

question: When does stopping distance increase?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases whenever traction is reduced or speed is higher. Wet, icy, snowy, or loose gravel roads reduce tire grip, so it takes more distance to stop. You should slow down and increase following distance in poor conditions to give yourself more space to brake safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Never cross them under any circumstance.,b:To turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make another permitted left turn when safe.,c:To pass a slow-moving vehicle.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally mean no passing. However, you may carefully cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make another permitted left turn when it is safe. You may not cross them just to pass another vehicle.

question: How can drivers avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.,b:Flash your lights to get their attention.,c:Never pass them.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots directly behind them and along both sides, especially on the right. To stay visible, avoid driving right beside them, pass promptly when it is safe, and never tailgate. If you cannot see the truck or bus driver’s mirrors, they likely cannot see you.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, you should:
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what is the correct way to return to the pavement?
options: a:Stop on the edge of the road.,b:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,c:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid sudden braking. When you have slowed and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement while checking for traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you avoid when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Using your turn signal to indicate your intention.,b:Checking for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.,c:Failing to check your side and rearview mirrors.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and use your turn signal. Failing to check your side and rearview mirrors is dangerous because you may not see vehicles already in or approaching the lane you want to enter.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Exit the roadway at a safe place and take a short nap.,b:Drink more coffee and keep driving.,c:Turn up the radio loudly to stay awake.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, the safe choice is to get off the road and rest. Exit the roadway at a safe place, such as a rest area, and take a short nap. Coffee, loud music, or opening windows do not reliably prevent drowsiness and can give a false sense of alertness.

question: Which is a trait of a defensive driver?
options: a:Reacting with anger and aggression.,b:Being passive and ignoring hazards.,c:Being alert and anticipating potential dangers.
note: A defensive driver stays alert, scans the road ahead, and anticipates what other road users might do. By predicting potential hazards early, a defensive driver has more time and space to react safely and avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:Drivers should make hand motions to decide who goes first.
note: At a four‑way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule prevents confusion and collisions by clearly deciding who goes first. If vehicles arrive at different times, the one that arrives first has the right‑of‑way.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can safely pass.,b:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.,c:Honk to warn the bicyclist to move over.
note: When passing a bicyclist, you should slow down and give them as much space as safely possible, following your state’s minimum passing distance (often at least 3 feet, more at higher speeds). Never drive in the bicycle lane to pass, and avoid honking in a way that could startle the rider and cause a loss of control.

question: How far ahead should you typically look while driving to avoid last-second braking or sudden turns?
options: a:About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.,b:One to three seconds ahead.,c:Five to seven seconds ahead.
note: You should scan the road about 10–15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. Looking this far ahead helps you spot hazards early, adjust your speed smoothly, and avoid sudden braking or sharp turns that can surprise other drivers.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side with the lightest traffic.,b:On the side where traffic is moving in the same direction.,c:On the side facing oncoming traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and react if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road, improving their safety.

question: What is 'highway hypnosis' and how does it occur?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,b:Improved focus from frequent rest stops.,c:Increased alertness after driving nonstop.,d:A condition caused by staring at the roadway for long periods which reduces active scanning.
note: Highway hypnosis is a drowsy, trance‑like state that can occur when you stare straight ahead at the road for long periods and stop actively scanning. Your mind drifts, your reactions slow, and you may not notice hazards, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: When should drivers use hand-to-hand (push/pull) steering?
options: a:Only when parking at low speed.,b:When avoiding a hazard at high speed.,c:During normal driving for smooth, controlled steering.
note: Hand‑to‑hand (push/pull) steering is recommended for most normal driving situations because it keeps both hands on the wheel and reduces the chance of oversteering. It is typically used at speeds above very low parking speeds, but it can also be used at lower speeds for smooth, controlled steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:
options: a:Flash your lights to signal oncoming drivers.,b:Use the shoulder to pass when available.,c:Use the lane belonging to oncoming traffic only if it is safe and legal to do so.
note: On a two‑lane, two‑way road, you may pass a slower vehicle only by briefly entering the oncoming traffic lane when it is clearly safe and legal. You must have enough clear distance to pass without speeding, cutting off the other driver, or forcing oncoming traffic to slow or swerve, and you must not pass where signs, markings, or hills/curves prohibit it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs legally indicate?
options: a:Suggested speeds for comfortable driving.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed.,c:The speed drivers should use in heavy traffic.,d:The recommended speed for trucks only.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must never drive faster than the posted maximum, and you must slow down below the limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, which is true?
options: a:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow traffic light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in or close to the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, when is passing safe?
options: a:Whenever the vehicle ahead is slower regardless of sight distance.,b:If your vehicle is faster than the one ahead.,c:Only when you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic and can clearly see ahead.,d:When you are able to clearly see the road ahead only.
note: Passing on a two-way, two-lane road is only safe when you can clearly see far enough ahead, there are no immediate hazards, and you can complete the pass and return fully to your lane before meeting any oncoming traffic. You must also obey all pavement markings and signs that may prohibit passing.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate other drivers to signal urgency.,b:Speed only when there are no police officers around.,c:Plan ahead and allow plenty of time so you do not need to speed or break rules.,d:Avoid confrontations, stay calm, and do not respond to aggressive behavior with aggression.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, plan your trips so you are not rushed, leave early, and expect delays. Stay calm, follow the speed limit, keep a safe following distance, and avoid reacting to other drivers’ mistakes with anger or retaliation.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks or buses?
options: a:A designated school zone near buses.,b:The blind spots around a truck or bus where other vehicles cannot be seen.,c:A prohibited parking zone.,d:A special speed zone for large vehicles.
note: The “No Zone” is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck or bus driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

question: What does a single dashed yellow center line mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may not pass.,c:Traffic in both directions may pass when safe.
note: A single dashed yellow center line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is dashed and there are no other restrictions, vehicles traveling in either direction may cross the line to pass, but only when it is legal, the lane is clear, and it is safe to do so.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It will make you fall asleep at the wheel.,b:It will decrease your accident risk.,c:It can reduce your ability to concentrate and focus on driving.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your reaction time. This makes it harder to notice hazards, judge distances and speeds, and make safe decisions. If you are very upset or stressed, calm down before driving.

question: Which describes a trait of a good defensive driver?
options: a:Laziness.,b:Skill and awareness to avoid hazards.,c:Passivity.
note: A good defensive driver stays alert, scans the road ahead, and anticipates potential hazards so they can react early and safely. This includes avoiding distractions, keeping safe following distances, and being prepared for the unexpected actions of other road users.

question: A driver ahead is distracted, driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?
options: a:Assume the driver will correct their behavior and follow closely.,b:Imitate the behavior to fit in with traffic flow.,c:Give the vehicle extra space by increasing your following distance.
note: When another driver is distracted, their chances of making sudden or unsafe moves are higher. By increasing your following distance and giving them extra space, you give yourself more time to react and reduce the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout you must slow down and yield to which of the following?
options: a:Vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Only to larger vehicles.,c:All of the above: vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians already in or entering the roundabout.,d:Bicyclists and pedestrians in the roundabout.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, including vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in crosswalks at the entrances and exits. Enter only when there is a safe gap so you do not force others to brake or swerve.

question: What color are guide (directional) signs?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Guide signs that give directions, distances, and route information are typically green with white letters and symbols. They help drivers navigate to cities, streets, exits, and highways.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:Even if it means driving off the pavement.,b:On a narrow bridge.,c:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
note: You may pass on the right only when it can be done safely and without leaving the paved roadway, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is a clear lane to the right, or on multi-lane roads where traffic moves in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver who travels much slower than the speed limit do if traffic is backing up behind them on a two-lane road?
options: a:Pull off the roadway when safe to let other vehicles pass.,b:Maintain current speed because they have the right-of-way.,c:Refuse to let others pass.
note: On a two-lane road, if you are driving much slower than the normal flow and traffic is backing up behind you, you should safely pull off the roadway or into a turnout area when available to let other vehicles pass. This helps prevent unsafe passing maneuvers and reduces the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:By looking in your rearview mirror.,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,c:By checking your side mirrors only.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; each side has a blind spot that mirrors cannot cover. To check blind spots before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check, combined with mirror use, ensures the lane is truly clear.

question: When is evasive-action steering used?
options: a:To quickly steer around a sudden hazard when braking alone may not prevent a collision.,b:For normal low-speed turns.,c:Only while parked.
note: Evasive steering is used when you must quickly steer around a sudden hazard, such as a stopped vehicle or debris, especially at higher speeds where hard braking alone may not prevent a collision. You steer smoothly but decisively into an open path, avoiding oversteering so you maintain control and stability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and turn only when it is safe.,b:Ignore the rearview mirror and rely only on the turn signal.,c:Signal several seconds in advance, get into the proper lane, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Before turning left, signal at least several seconds (and about 100 feet in city driving, more at higher speeds) before the turn, move into the proper lane, and slow down. Check your mirrors and blind spots, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and complete the turn only when it is safe.

question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Obeying posted speed limits.,c:Using proper turn signals.,d:All of the above
note: Allowing extra travel time reduces pressure to rush, obeying speed limits keeps traffic more predictable, and using proper turn signals helps other drivers anticipate your actions. Together, these habits lower frustration for you and others, which helps prevent road rage and aggressive driving situations.

question: When following an emergency vehicle, what minimum following distance should you keep?
options: a:Four seconds.,b:Ten seconds.,c:Two seconds.
note: When following an emergency vehicle, you should leave extra space so it can stop, turn, or maneuver suddenly. A following distance of at least four seconds gives you more time to react and reduces the risk of a rear-end collision if the emergency vehicle brakes or changes direction unexpectedly.

question: If someone is injured in an accident, you should:
options: a:Always leave the injured where they are and do nothing.,b:Not move the injured unnecessarily and keep them warm while providing first aid.,c:Move the injured person immediately away from the scene.
note: If someone is injured in a crash, do not move them unless there is immediate danger such as fire, explosion, or oncoming traffic you cannot control. Moving an injured person unnecessarily can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Keep them warm, reassure them, and provide first aid only if you are trained, while waiting for emergency medical help.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and begins to lose traction, what is the correct braking technique?
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer.
note: With Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and let the system automatically pump the brakes for you. Keep steady pressure on the pedal and steer in the direction you want to go. Do not pump the brakes yourself, because that can interfere with the ABS and reduce your ability to steer while braking hard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do before proceeding?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,b:Drive slowly to let approaching vehicles get out of the way.,c:Honk to alert others.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb line and yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic. Proceed only when it is safe and clear. Drivers entering the roadway from a driveway do not have the right-of-way over pedestrians or vehicles already on the road.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the S represent?
options: a:Sweep, Search and Scan.,b:Stare ahead.,c:Slow down.
note: In the SIPDE process, the S stands for Sweep, Search, and Scan. This means you should constantly move your eyes and check all around your vehicle—far ahead, to the sides, and behind—to spot potential hazards early and give yourself more time to react.

question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct response?
options: a:Brake hard and stop immediately.,b:Turn sharply back onto the road at full speed.,c:Take your foot off the accelerator,d:Accelerate and quickly jerk the wheel back on the pavement.
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and do not brake hard or jerk the wheel. Gently ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, and let the vehicle slow down in a controlled way. When your speed is reduced and the shoulder is stable, carefully steer back onto the roadway with small, smooth steering inputs.

question: When must you stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children?
options: a:Only if the bus displays no passengers.,b:If you are on a two-lane highway and the bus's red lights are flashing.,c:Only if you are on the same side and the bus is on the shoulder.
note: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and/or stop arm extended, regardless of whether the bus is on the shoulder or in the lane. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, then proceed with extra caution for children nearby.

question: From which areas of your vehicle should snow and ice be removed before driving?
options: a:Only the windshield and passenger window.,b:All windows,c:Just the windshield.
note: Remove all snow and ice from windows, hood, roof, and mirrors so you have clear visibility and to prevent ice or snow from falling onto other vehicles.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow and white.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow pavement markings are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the edges of the roadway. When you see a yellow centerline, expect oncoming traffic on the other side.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,b:Stop if a train is nearby,c:Drive faster than a train.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks and must be ready to slow or stop. Look and listen for trains in both directions, obey flashing lights, bells, and gates, and never drive around lowered gates. If a train is approaching or signals are active, you must stop at a safe distance and wait until it is completely safe to cross.

question: What will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Only the passage of time.,c:Tomato juice and lime.
note: Nothing you eat or drink can quickly sober you up. Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol, lowering your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, cold showers, or other home remedies may make you feel more awake, but they do not reduce impairment or make it safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.,b:You are not required to stop in that case.,c:Only slow down and proceed if clear.,d:Stop at the center of the intersection.
note: When there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can clearly see approaching traffic. This lets you obey the stop requirement while still being able to check for cross traffic safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you have the legal right-of-way at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Speed up to get through the intersection quickly.,b:Wave other drivers forward to indicate your intent.,c:Proceed cautiously; do not assume other drivers will obey right-of-way rules.
note: Having the legal right-of-way never guarantees that other drivers will yield. You should enter intersections only after checking that cross traffic is stopping or yielding as required, and be prepared to slow or stop if another driver makes a mistake.

question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is correct?
options: a:You should always follow closely behind them.,b:They never use loudspeakers.,c:You do not need to yield if they are on the other side of the street.,d:They have the right-of-way when using sirens and/or flashing lights.
note: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping when safe. Stay clear of the vehicle’s path and follow any instructions given over a loudspeaker.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem indicate?
options: a:The vehicle is a commercial truck.,b:The vehicle will travel faster than the speed limit.,c:The vehicle is likely traveling 25 mph or slower (reflective orange triangle).
note: A reflective orange triangle on the rear of a vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle emblem. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, so you should be prepared to slow down and only pass when it is legal and safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle on a two-lane road?
options: a:In a curve or on a hill if it looks clear.,b:By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.,c:Only when there is no oncoming traffic and the passing maneuver is not prohibited by pavement markings.
note: On a two-lane road, you may only pass when there is enough clear distance ahead, no oncoming traffic, and passing is not prohibited by signs or pavement markings. You must never pass on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, and you may not pass by driving onto the shoulder.

question: Which winter driving statement is NOT true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,c:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels before winter travel.
note: In winter, roads can be icy, snowy, and slippery, making it one of the most difficult and hazardous driving seasons. You should check antifreeze and washer fluid before winter trips, and you should NOT use cruise control on snow, ice, or in heavy rain because it can reduce your control if the vehicle starts to skid.

question: When driving near a motorcycle, what should you allow?
options: a:To ride on the shoulder next to you.,b:The motorcycle a full lane width.,c:To be passed in the same lane with you.,d:To use only half a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane just like any other motor vehicle. You should never try to share a lane with a motorcycle or pass it within the same lane. Give motorcycles the full lane width and extra following distance because they are smaller and more vulnerable.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, how should you respond?
options: a:Flash your lights and argue with them.,b:Attempt to block or retaliate.,c:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm and avoid any actions that could escalate the situation. Do not flash your lights, honk aggressively, or try to block or retaliate. Instead, slow down, create space, let them go ahead, and if necessary have a passenger report the driver to authorities when it is safe.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Assume trains will yield to your vehicle.,b:Drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.,c:Obey signals and look both ways before crossing tracks.
note: At light rail or train crossings, you must always obey all warning signs, signals, and gates. Look carefully both ways along the tracks before crossing, and never drive around lowered gates, even if you do not see a train, because another train may be approaching or the train may be closer than it appears.

question: Where should you maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only behind your vehicle.,c:Only in front of your vehicle.
note: You should keep a space cushion on all sides of your vehicle—front, rear, and sides. Extra space gives you time and room to react if another driver brakes suddenly, changes lanes, or opens a door, and it reduces the chance of a collision.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection mean?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way; be prepared to stop if necessary.,b:Always come to a full stop.,c:Slow only if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangular sign is a yield sign. You must slow down and be ready to stop, yielding the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection. Stop if needed to avoid interfering with other road users.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what assumption should you make?
options: a:Slam on your brakes as you pass.,b:Speed up to get past quickly.,c:Assume the driver may open a door into the roadway.
note: When passing a vehicle parked at the curb, you should assume someone might open a door or step out into the roadway. Slow slightly, be ready to brake, and leave as much space as safely possible to avoid a sudden door opening or pedestrian.

question: A steady yellow arrow displayed at an intersection tells drivers to:
options: a:Merge into the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Proceed with caution and turn without yielding.,c:Stop if it is safe to do so because a red arrow is coming.,d:Ignore the arrow and follow the circular light.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected turning movement is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should stop if you can do so safely. If you are already too close to stop safely, you may complete the turn with caution before the light turns red.

question: At night, which of the following is the hardest to see while driving?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Other motorists.
note: At night, pedestrians are the hardest to see because they are smaller, often wear dark clothing, and may not be illuminated by headlights until you are very close. Road signs and other vehicles are usually lit or reflective, so they are easier to detect.

question: Which is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Perception time.,b:Steering ability.,c:Braking distance.,d:Reaction distance.
note: Total stopping distance is made up of three parts: perception distance (how far you travel while you recognize a hazard), reaction distance (how far you travel while you move your foot to the brake), and braking distance (how far you travel after you apply the brakes until you stop). Steering ability does not directly change how long it takes the vehicle to stop in a straight line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic light at an intersection warns you to:
options: a:Go if the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before the intersection. Only continue through if you are already so close that stopping safely is not possible without hard braking or skidding.

question: How should you drive on slippery roads?
options: a:Drive with emergency flashers on.,b:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.,c:Reduce speed and avoid sudden changes; do not use cruise control.,d:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: On slippery roads, you need extra traction and time to react. Reduce your speed, make all steering, braking, and accelerating movements gently, and avoid sudden changes. Do not use cruise control, because it can cause the wheels to spin or lose traction before you can react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A flashing green light.,b:A yellow arrow.,c:A flashing red light.,d:A steady yellow light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop, look for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Keep a steady pace and let them adjust.,b:Maintain your position in the blind spot to stay hidden.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you stay in these areas, the driver may change lanes or turn into your path. Either move ahead or drop back so that you are clearly visible in the other driver’s mirrors.

question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a lane indicate?
options: a:Lanes travel in the same direction and you may pass when safe.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes travel in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The combination can multiply or increase the impairing effects of either the alcohol or the medication.
note: Alcohol can interact with both prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines so that each one makes the other more impairing. Together they can greatly reduce your coordination, judgment, and reaction time, making driving extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging from an entrance ramp onto a highway, you should generally:
options: a:Enter above the speed of traffic to get ahead.,b:Use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic and merge safely into a gap.,c:Enter slowly and immediately move to the left lane.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to build up speed so you match the flow of traffic on the highway. Signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and merge into a suitable gap without stopping if traffic allows.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign represent?
options: a:A mere recommendation only for bad weather.,b:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions for that roadway.,c:The exact speed you must always travel to avoid a ticket.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed for that road in ideal conditions. If conditions are poor—such as rain, fog, heavy traffic, or road work—you must slow down to a speed that is safe, even if it is below the posted limit.

question: When an oncoming vehicle approaches at night, your headlights should be:
options: a:On the high beam setting.,b:Off; use parking lights instead.,c:On the low beam setting.
note: When another vehicle is approaching at night, you must switch to low beams to avoid blinding the other driver with glare. High beams are only for use when there is no oncoming traffic and you are not following another vehicle closely.

question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
options: a:Make turning more difficult.,b:Increase the likelihood of hydroplaning.,c:Increase your stopping distance.,d:All of the above
note: Worn or bald tires have less tread, which reduces their grip on the road. This makes it harder for the tires to channel water away, increasing the risk of hydroplaning, and it lengthens your stopping distance because there is less friction. Poor tread also reduces traction when turning, making cornering more difficult and less stable.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and/or siren, you must:
options: a:Only pull over if it is coming from the opposite direction.,b:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop,c:Only pull over if it is following you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb and stopping until it has passed. This applies whether the vehicle is coming from ahead or behind, unless directed otherwise by a police officer or if you are in an intersection, in which case you clear the intersection first and then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights at the vehicle ahead before passing.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear before changing lanes.,c:Always pass on the right.
note: On a multilane highway, you should only move into a passing lane after you have checked that the lane is clear ahead and behind, signaled, and confirmed there is enough space to pass safely. Most passing is done on the left; passing on the right is only allowed when it can be done safely and is not prohibited, such as when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is enough room to pass on the right without leaving the roadway.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards?
options: a:Look only as far as the car in front of you.,b:Keep both feet lightly on the brake and stare at the rearview mirror.,c:Continuously scan the entire roadway and both roadsides ahead and around you.,d:Stare straight ahead at the center of the road.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check mirrors regularly. Looking well ahead and around you helps you spot hazards early, such as slowing traffic, pedestrians, or vehicles entering from side streets, so you have time to adjust speed or change lanes smoothly instead of reacting at the last second.

question: Where is parking prohibited among the listed options?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is not allowed on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because it blocks pedestrians and cyclists and creates a safety hazard. When parking on the street where it is allowed, you must park parallel and close to the curb (typically within about 12 inches) and obey all posted parking signs and markings.

question: If you are emotionally upset (worried, angry, or crying), you should:
options: a:Take time to calm and refocus before driving.,b:Expect to drive the same as you would normally.,c:Start driving immediately to get it over with.
note: Strong emotions like anger, worry, or crying can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to poor decisions behind the wheel. You should wait until you have calmed down and can focus fully on driving before you start your trip.

question: On average, how much time does the body need to eliminate one standard alcoholic drink?
options: a:Three hours.,b:Two hours.,c:One hour.
note: As a general guideline, the body takes about one hour to process the alcohol in a single standard drink, though this can vary by person and situation. Even after that time, you may still be impaired, so never rely on timing alone to decide if it is safe to drive.

question: What types of drugs can affect your driving ability?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only strong cold remedies.,c:Prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can all affect your driving ability.
note: Many different drugs can impair driving, including prescription medications, over‑the‑counter medicines like some cold remedies, and illegal drugs. Always read medication labels and talk with your doctor or pharmacist about whether it is safe to drive while taking them.

question: When a transit bus is signaling to reenter traffic after a passenger stop, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Yield to the bus by changing lanes, slowing, or stopping to allow it to safely merge.,b:Honk to tell the bus driver you are there.,c:Speed up so the bus cannot merge in front of you.
note: When a transit bus signals that it is pulling away from a stop, you should cooperate and allow it to reenter traffic safely. Adjust your speed or change lanes if possible so the bus can merge without sudden braking or swerving.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It lessens alcohol's effects on driving ability.,c:It decreases the risk of causing a crash.
note: Combining alcohol with any other drug—whether prescription, over‑the‑counter, or illegal—can greatly increase drowsiness, confusion, and poor coordination. This multiplies your level of impairment and significantly raises the risk of causing a crash.

question: Which of the following statements about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Ensure all passengers are properly restrained,b:You should never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with an active airbag.,c:All of the above,d:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child in a front-facing crash even at low speeds.
note: Seat belts and child restraints must be used for every passenger on every trip. Infants and small children should never be placed in the front seat of a vehicle with an active airbag because airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure or kill a child, especially in a front-facing crash and even at low speeds. Children are safest properly restrained in the rear seat, using the correct child safety seat or booster for their size and age.

question: What do hurricane evacuation route signs indicate?
options: a:They are intended only for out-of-state drivers.,b:The highway is a designated evacuation route to be used during a hurricane.,c:They are only posted during an active hurricane.
note: Evacuation route signs show roads that are planned and designated for use during emergencies such as hurricanes. Knowing these routes ahead of time helps you leave an area quickly and safely when officials issue an evacuation order.

question: Anything that causes you to take your eyes off the road, hands off the wheel, or attention away from driving can:
options: a:Improve your driving concentration.,b:Help you react faster.,c:Increase the chance of a crash.
note: Anything that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving is a distraction. Distractions slow your reaction time and make it easier to miss hazards, which greatly increases your chances of being involved in a crash.

question: When stopped at an intersection, which way should you look before proceeding?
options: a:To your left, then right, then left again while also checking straight ahead and, when appropriate, behind you for hazards.,b:Only to your right.,c:Straight ahead only.,d:Only to your left.
note: Before moving into an intersection, you should scan in all directions: left, right, and ahead, and check again to the left where traffic enters your lane first. This helps you see vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists that may be entering from any side and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers first.,c:Immediately turn on high beams.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, fog, darkness, or other conditions, your first response should be to slow down. Lower speed gives you more time to see and react to hazards. Then, as needed, you can also use headlights and wipers to improve your ability to see and be seen.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct immediate action?
options: a:Shift to neutral, apply steady braking, and pull safely off the road before turning off the engine.,b:Reach down immediately to pull up the accelerator.,c:Shift directly into park while moving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road, shift to neutral so the engine is no longer driving the wheels, apply steady firm braking, and steer to the side of the road. Once you are safely off the roadway and under control, then turn off the engine. Do not reach down to pull up the pedal or shift into park while moving, as you can lose control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Slow and proceed if clear.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,c:Stop before the intersection and remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. You must remain stopped until the light turns green and it is safe to proceed. You may not just slow and go, and you must stop whether or not pedestrians are present.

question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, how should you behave?
options: a:Proceed normally and expect them to yield.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Slow down well in advance, be prepared to stop, and do not honk or rev your engine. Blind pedestrians rely on sound cues, so give them extra time and space to cross safely.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must do what?
options: a:Copy the actions of surrounding vehicles regardless of the guard.,b:Speed through if no children are visible.,c:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,d:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to direct traffic in school zones. You must obey their instructions, even if they differ from traffic signals, and drive with extra caution and reduced speed as directed to protect children and other pedestrians.

question: When you notice other drivers acting angrily or aggressively, what is the appropriate reaction?
options: a:Do not engage—avoid eye contact, do not react, and distance yourself.,b:Make eye contact to show you mean no harm.,c:Respond with similar hand gestures to defuse the situation.
note: When you encounter an angry or aggressive driver, your goal is to avoid conflict. Do not make eye contact or respond with gestures. Instead, stay calm, slow down or change lanes if safe, and create distance between your vehicle and the aggressive driver.

question: If you encounter a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,b:Come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping if clear.,d:Treat it like a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield the right‑of‑way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Approximately what percentage of crashes occur within 25 miles of home?
options: a:90 percent.,b:75 percent.,c:50 percent.,d:25 percent.
note: Crash statistics commonly show that the vast majority of collisions happen close to home, often around 90% within a relatively short distance. This is why you must always wear your seat belt and stay alert, even on short, familiar trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which driver goes first?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived last has the right-of-way.,b:The first vehicle to arrive at the intersection has the right-of-way.,c:Vehicles should proceed in numerical order of their license plates.
note: At a four‑way stop, the driver who stops first has the right‑of‑way and goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always proceed cautiously and be prepared to yield if another driver moves unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain the same speed and position.,b:Slow down to give space in front of your vehicle for the pass.,c:Speed up to prevent the pass.
note: If another driver wants to pass you, you should help the pass occur safely. Gently reduce your speed to create more space in front of your vehicle so the passing driver has a larger, safer gap to move back into the lane. Never speed up to block a pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
