question: While waiting in an intersection to finish a left turn, what should you do with your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights to alert drivers.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead while your turn signal is on. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. Keeping the wheels straight reduces this risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection to turn but are not in the correct lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: If you are not in the correct lane to make a turn, you must not turn from the wrong lane or cut across traffic. Continue straight, go to the next intersection, and make your turn from the proper lane. Sudden lane changes or turns from the wrong lane can cause crashes.

question: In a city, you should look how many blocks ahead of your vehicle?
options: a:One block.,b:Three blocks.,c:Two blocks.
note: In city driving, you should scan about one to two blocks, or 10–15 seconds, ahead of your vehicle so you can see traffic signals, pedestrians, and hazards early and have time to react safely. Looking too short a distance ahead reduces your time to respond.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you start a left turn from a multilane one-way street?
options: a:The leftmost lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The right lane.,d:The lane marked for right turns only.
note: When turning left from a multilane one‑way street, you should start from the leftmost lane unless signs or lane markings direct you otherwise. Starting from the correct lane keeps traffic organized and reduces the chance of sideswipe or turning collisions.

question: The effect of lack of sleep on driving ability is comparable to which of the following?
options: a:The effect of anger.,b:The effect of amphetamines.,c:The effect of being under the influence of alcohol.
note: Being very tired or sleep‑deprived can slow your reaction time, impair judgment, and reduce awareness in ways similar to being under the influence of alcohol. Driving while drowsy is dangerous and can lead to crashes just as impaired driving can.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,b:The amount you drink.,c:Your body weight.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight and metabolism. The type or brand of alcoholic beverage does not change the amount of pure alcohol you consume if the total alcohol content is the same.

question: How is defensive driving most accurately described?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself by getting ahead of other drivers.,c:Following closely behind the vehicle ahead to control traffic.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning for potential hazards, predicting what might happen, and adjusting your speed, position, or actions early to avoid conflicts and crashes. It is not about being aggressive or trying to control other drivers.

question: Before turning the ignition on, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.,b:Make sure all occupants, including the driver, have fastened their seat belts.,c:Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.,d:Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
note: Develop a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seat belt and ensure all passengers do likewise.

question: When children are in a vehicle, what is the safest practice?
options: a:Keep them standing on the vehicle floor.,b:Use proper child seats or restraints and never hold a child during travel.,c:Hold them securely in an adult's lap.
note: Children must always be secured in an appropriate child safety seat or restraint system for their age, height, and weight. Holding a child in your arms or lap is extremely dangerous because, in a crash, you cannot physically hold onto them against the force of impact.

question: Which factor does NOT affect vehicle stopping distance?
options: a:Your reaction time.,b:Condition of the vehicle's brakes.,c:Time of day.,d:Roadway conditions.
note: Stopping distance is the distance your vehicle travels from the moment you see a hazard until you come to a complete stop. It depends on your perception and reaction time, your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the road surface. The time of day by itself does not directly change how far the vehicle needs to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, what is the correct action to warn other drivers?
options: a:Use your four-way flashers (hazard lights) to warn other drivers.,b:Sound your horn at passing motorists.,c:Sit in your car and wait for help.
note: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, you should move as far off the roadway as possible and immediately turn on your four‑way flashers (hazard lights) so other drivers can see that your vehicle is stopped. Staying in a live traffic lane without warning others is extremely dangerous. Use hazard lights and, if safe, additional signals like raising the hood or placing reflective triangles.

question: If there are two parallel railroad tracks, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:Assume it is safe to proceed immediately.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for another train on the adjacent track before crossing.
note: When there are two or more tracks, one train can hide another that is approaching on the next track. After one train passes, do not assume the crossing is clear. Look and listen carefully for another train on any track and only proceed when you are sure all tracks are clear.

question: If involved in a serious crash, what should you do first?
options: a:Only call your insurance company and ignore injuries.,b:Continue driving if no one seems to notice.,c:Stop and assist—check for injuries and call 911 if necessary.
note: In a serious crash, you must stop immediately, protect the scene as best you can, and check for injuries. Call 911 if anyone is hurt or if there is significant damage. Rendering reasonable assistance and notifying emergency services is both a legal duty and a critical safety step.

question: Which of these does NOT typically promote safe night driving?
options: a:Be aware that tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.,b:Keep your windshield clean.,c:Rely on a flashlight while driving.
note: Safe night driving depends on maximizing your ability to see and be seen. Keeping your windshield clean and understanding that tinted windows reduce visibility at night both help you drive more safely. Relying on a handheld flashlight while driving is unsafe and not a proper driving technique; you should rely on your vehicle’s headlights and properly maintained windows and mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must use your turn signal in which situation?
options: a:Only when other traffic is present.,b:When changing lanes.,c:When pulling into traffic from a curbside parking space or alley.,d:When driving straight on a highway.
note: Turn signals must be used any time you intend to move left or right, including when changing lanes and when pulling into traffic from a curb, driveway, or alley. Signaling lets other road users anticipate your movement and helps prevent collisions. You should signal even if you do not see other traffic, because vehicles or pedestrians may be present that you have not noticed.

question: What is the most important rule for managing speed in curves?
options: a:Accelerate just before entering the curve.,b:Maintain posted speed until the sharpest part of the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve so you can steer smoothly and stay in your lane. Entering too fast makes it harder to control the vehicle because inertia wants to keep you going straight, which can cause skidding or drifting into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your car be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As far to the right side of the street as possible.,d:In the middle lane.
note: When making a right turn, move your vehicle as close to the right edge or curb as is safe, without driving into a bike lane unless it is specifically allowed. This position shortens the turn, keeps you predictable, and reduces the chance of another vehicle passing on your right.

question: Which headlights should you use while driving in fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.,d:Hazard lights only.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and help you see lane lines and the edge of the roadway more clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, what are they signaling?
options: a:They intend to turn left.,b:They intend to turn right.,c:They are coming to a stop.
note: Standard hand signals use the left arm: left arm straight out means a left turn, left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. The upward position is used so drivers behind you can see the signal clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a green arrow signal mean?
options: a:You may proceed in any direction indicated by other lanes.,b:Traffic may proceed in the direction of the arrow although vehicles must turn in that direction.,c:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow from that lane, and you must turn in that direction if you are in the turn lane. You may proceed only if the intersection is clear of pedestrians and other vehicles.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Drivers must exercise due care to avoid colliding with pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against a signal.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,d:Only at intersections controlled by traffic lights.
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid colliding with pedestrians, even when pedestrians are crossing illegally or carelessly. However, the law does not give pedestrians the right of way in every situation, such as when they suddenly leave a curb and enter the path of a vehicle so close that the driver cannot reasonably yield. You must slow, be prepared to stop, and do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, but pedestrians also have responsibilities to obey signals and not enter traffic unsafely.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Slow down but not stop.,b:Proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Stop completely and yield to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, look for other vehicles, pedestrians, and bicycles, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A center lane marked for special use typically allows drivers to:
options: a:Make left turns from that lane.,b:Pass slow-moving traffic.,c:Use it for through traffic.
note: A center lane marked for left turns is a shared lane used only for making left turns from either direction, not for passing or driving straight through. Enter the lane shortly before your turn, signal, and wait for a safe gap before turning.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze first in cold or wet conditions?
options: a:On the crest of hills only.,b:On flat open roadways.,c:On bridges, overpasses, and in shaded areas such as those under trees or next to buildings.,d:In areas receiving direct sun.
note: Shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, on bridges and overpasses, or next to buildings, tend to freeze before other areas and stay icy longer because they receive less direct sunlight. In cold or wet weather, reduce speed and be especially cautious on bridges, overpasses, and shaded sections where black ice can form even when the rest of the road looks clear.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, what is the correct action?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Always stop before crossing even if no train is visible.,c:Be prepared to yield to any approaching train and do not cross until the way is clear.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Never enter the tracks unless you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to completely clear the tracks on the other side.

question: When may you park or stop along the freeway shoulder?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road and there is no emergency.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,c:If you turn on four-way flashers it is permitted.,d:Whenever you need to read a map.
note: Parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder is only allowed for emergencies, such as a breakdown, medical issue, or when directed by law enforcement. You may not use the shoulder to stop for rest, phone calls, reading a map, or other non‑emergency reasons, even if your vehicle is completely off the travel lanes.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Circle.,b:Rectangle.,c:Octagon.
note: A stop sign is the only standard road sign that is an octagon (eight sides). Its unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly, even if visibility is poor or the sign is partially blocked, and it always means you must come to a complete stop before proceeding when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, what sequence should you perform?
options: a:Check mirrors and then change lanes without signaling.,b:Signal and immediately change lanes.,c:Signal only.,d:Check mirrors only.
note: Before changing lanes, you should follow this sequence: first signal to show your intention, then check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and change lanes only when it is safe. Signaling alone is not enough; you must also check traffic around you before moving.

question: As a pedestrian, what should you do when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Enter the crosswalk because drivers must stop for you.,b:Always demand right-of-way in a crosswalk.,c:Do not enter the street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
note: Even when you have the right‑of‑way as a pedestrian, you should not step into the street or crosswalk if vehicles are so close that they may not be able to stop in time. Make sure approaching drivers see you and have enough distance to stop safely before you begin crossing.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,b:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Roads are usually most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm. Water mixes with oil and other residues on the road surface, creating a slick layer. After it has rained longer, much of this buildup is washed away and traction generally improves, though you should still drive carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver is following you too closely on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down but stay in your lane.,b:Move into another lane to let the car pass.,c:Speed up to increase distance.
note: If another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to create space and let them pass. On a multilane highway, signal and move to a lane on the right when it is safe, allowing the tailgater to go by. Do not speed up, because that only increases your own risk and does not solve the tailgating problem.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Sound your horn before starting your lane change.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check mirrors and blind spot, signal, and change lanes only when safe.
note: Before changing lanes, you must make sure the lane is clear by checking your mirrors and briefly looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then signaling and moving only when safe. Simply sounding your horn or turning on headlights is not a proper substitute for checking traffic around you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you reduce your speed below the posted limit?
options: a:Only when entering a highway with other cars.,b:Whenever conditions such as weather, traffic, or visibility make the posted speed unsafe.,c:Only when you see a police officer.
note: You must drive at a speed that is safe for current conditions, even if that means going below the posted speed limit. In rain, snow, fog, heavy traffic, poor road surfaces, or limited visibility, you are required to slow down and can be cited for driving too fast for conditions even while under the limit.

question: What is the proper initial step when parallel parking between two vehicles?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,b:Pull up even with the vehicle in front of the space.,c:Back in at full speed to clear the space quickly.
note: When parallel parking, you first stop your vehicle parallel and even with the car in front of the space, leaving a safe gap. Then you signal, check traffic, and begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as appropriate. You should never back in quickly or turn the wheels immediately without setting up your position.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your judgment of speed and distance is improved.,b:You become less alert.,c:Your reflexes slow down.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes, reduces alertness, and impairs judgment, including your ability to judge speed and distance. It never improves these abilities. Because of this, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: What is the purpose of a yellow-and-black diamond-shaped sign?
options: a:Indicate a speed limit change.,b:Warn drivers about conditions on or near the road ahead.,c:Help direct you to upcoming cities and towns.
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs with black symbols are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings, so you can slow down and be prepared.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It only increases pollution and is not a health risk.,b:It reduces seat belt effectiveness.,c:It causes a loss of hearing.,d:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is a colorless, odorless gas that can quickly cause sickness, unconsciousness, or death, so exhaust leaks must be repaired immediately.

question: What is the best way to avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Simply refuse a drink by saying you are driving.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Call a taxi after you have been drinking.
note: The safest way to avoid an alcohol-related crash is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Because alcohol impairs judgment, you cannot rely on making a safe decision about driving after you have already been drinking.

question: When passing a large truck or bus, what effect should a driver of a small vehicle be ready for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Wind gusts from the large vehicle.,c:Excess air pollution.
note: When passing a large truck or bus, be prepared for strong wind gusts that can push or pull your smaller vehicle sideways. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and allow extra space as you pass to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Signal only if another vehicle is present.,b:Signal only after initiating the maneuver.,c:Always signal your intentions even if no visible traffic is present.,d:Signal only at night.
note: You must always signal when turning, changing lanes, entering traffic, or pulling away from a curb, even if you do not see other vehicles or pedestrians. Signaling clearly gives others time to react and helps prevent collisions.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,d:Exercise.
note: The only way to lower your BAC is to wait for your body to metabolize and eliminate the alcohol over time. Coffee, cold showers, and exercise might make you feel more awake, but they do not speed up how quickly your liver processes alcohol, so they do not reduce BAC.

question: Driving down a long or steep hill, what should you monitor?
options: a:Assume all traffic maintains a constant speed.,b:Ignore large trucks.,c:Check your mirrors for traffic building up behind you.
note: On long or steep downgrades, you should regularly check your mirrors to see if traffic is building up behind you, especially large trucks that may gain speed downhill. This helps you adjust your speed or change lanes safely so faster traffic can pass.

question: If another driver is passing your car, what should you do to help them complete the pass safely?
options: a:Pull off the road immediately.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter the lane.,c:Signal aggressively to warn them.,d:Brake suddenly to prevent the pass.
note: When another driver is passing you, help them by maintaining a steady speed or slightly reducing your speed so they have enough space and time to pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly; keep watching the road ahead so the passing driver can return to the lane safely.

question: What describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Someone who daydreams or stares at objects off the roadway instead of scanning the road.,b:A driver who maintains eye contact with a passenger while talking.,c:Someone who looks only at the car directly ahead.
note: An inattentive driver is not fully focused on the driving task, such as someone who is daydreaming or staring at things off the roadway instead of scanning the road ahead and checking mirrors. Good drivers keep their eyes moving and avoid distractions from passengers or objects inside and outside the vehicle.

question: In winter, how do shaded areas on the road behave compared to the rest of the roadway?
options: a:They freeze after the rest of the road.,b:They behave the same as the rest of the road.,c:They tend to freeze before and stay icy longer than other areas.
note: In winter, shaded areas of the road, such as those under trees, on bridges, or in tunnels, tend to freeze before the rest of the roadway and stay icy longer because they get less sunlight. Drivers should slow down and use extra caution when approaching these areas in cold weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:
options: a:Force other vehicles to make room because they are on the ramp.,b:Assume they have right-of-way over interstate traffic.,c:Yield to vehicles already on the interstate and merge when safe.
note: When entering an interstate, you must yield to traffic already on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Vehicles on the interstate have the right-of-way.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Over your left shoulder.,c:Only at your left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes to the left, check your mirrors and then glance over your left shoulder to see the area your mirrors do not cover. This quick shoulder check reveals vehicles in your left blind spot so you do not move into an occupied lane.

question: Compared with daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No different in terms of risk.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous because visibility is reduced and hazards are harder to see.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because you can see less distance ahead, making it harder to spot hazards, pedestrians, and road signs. Glare from headlights, driver fatigue, and a higher likelihood of impaired drivers also increase the risk compared with daytime driving.

question: Which measures help prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Making sure your tires have good tread depth.,b:Keeping your tires properly inflated.,c:Reducing speed in rainy conditions.,d:All of the above
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. You can reduce this risk by keeping tires properly inflated, maintaining good tread depth so water can be channeled away, and slowing down in wet conditions so your tires can maintain grip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green arrow on a signal allow drivers to do?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow without yielding.,b:Stop and wait for a green circular light before turning.,c:Turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed to turn after ensuring the intersection is clear and yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection, but oncoming traffic and conflicting movements are normally stopped by a red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when are you allowed to cross them?
options: a:Under no circumstances at all.,b:To pass another vehicle if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Only to make a left turn into or out of an alley, driveway, side road, or private property.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and mean you must not cross them to pass. However, you may carefully cross double solid yellow lines to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, side road, or private property when it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a stated instruction are called what?
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations you must obey, such as speed limits, stop or yield requirements, lane use, and parking rules. Ignoring a regulatory sign is the same as breaking a traffic law.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Upcoming railroad crossings.,c:No passing zones.
note: Round traffic signs are used specifically to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing. When you see a round railroad warning sign, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana's GDL program, what passenger restrictions apply to an Intermediate License holder between the hours of 6:00 PM and 5:00 AM?
options: a:No passengers under age 21 are allowed,b:No more than one passenger under age 21 who is not immediate family is allowed (unless accompanied by a licensed adult age 21 or older),c:Only family members are allowed as passengers,d:No passenger restrictions apply
note: In Louisiana, intermediate license holders are prohibited from transporting more than one passenger under age 21 who is not a member of the immediate family between the hours of 6:00 PM and 5:00 AM, unless accompanied by a licensed adult.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the driving curfew for an unaccompanied Intermediate License holder under age 17 in Louisiana?
options: a:10:00 PM to 5:00 AM,b:11:00 PM to 5:00 AM,c:Midnight to 5:00 AM,d:12:30 AM to 5:00 AM
note: Louisiana intermediate license holders under age 17 are prohibited from driving unaccompanied between the hours of 11:00 PM and 5:00 AM, unless driving to or from a school- or work-related activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum auto liability insurance coverage limits required for all motor vehicles registered in Louisiana?
note: Louisiana law requires all vehicle owners to maintain minimum liability insurance coverage of 15/30/25: $15,000 for bodily injury per person, $30,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana law, you are required to report a motor vehicle crash to the police or local authorities if it results in injury, death, or total property damage exceeding:
note: Louisiana law (R.S. 32:398) requires drivers to report any traffic accident to local authorities immediately if it results in injury, death, or property damage in excess of $500.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana's Move Over law, if you are driving on a two-lane road and approach a stationary emergency vehicle on the shoulder, you must slow to:
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: Louisiana's Move Over law requires drivers on a two-lane road to slow down to a speed of 25 miles per hour (or the posted speed limit, whichever is lower) when passing stopped emergency or utility vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana law, what is the minimum age at which a child is legally permitted to ride in the open bed of a pickup truck?
options: a:10 years old,b:12 years old,c:15 years old,d:16 years old
note: Louisiana law prohibits any person from permitting a child under the age of 12 years to ride as a passenger in the open bed of a pickup truck or utility vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana law, what is the maximum speed limit for any vehicle pulling or towing another motor vehicle on a highway?
options: a:45 mph,b:50 mph,c:55 mph,d:60 mph
note: In Louisiana, the maximum speed limit for any vehicle pulling or towing another motor vehicle is 45 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Louisiana's implied consent law, what is the penalty for a first-time refusal to submit to a chemical test for blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:A 90-day driver's license suspension,b:A 180-day driver's license suspension,c:A 1-year driver's license suspension,d:A $1,000 fine and 10 days in jail
note: If you refuse to submit to a chemical test for BAC in Louisiana, your driving privileges will be suspended for 180 days on your first offense.
